items.title: Digital phenotyping for monitoring mental health outcomes in patients with cancer: a scoping review.
items.authors: Li X, Gong C, Li H, Yang H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Patients with cancer often experience anxiety, depression, psychological distress, and fear throughout diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. Conventional mental health assessment relies mainly on periodic clinical evaluations and patient-reported measures, which may increase patient burden and inadequately capture dynamic psychological changes in daily life. Digital phenotyping enables the passive and continuous collection of behavioral and physiological data through smartphones, wearable devices, and other sensors; however, evidence for its application to mental health in patients with cancer remains limited and fragmented.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PubMed, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from inception to July 2026 using terms related to digital phenotyping and cancer. A supplementary targeted sensitivity search was also conducted. Two reviewers independently screened the records and extracted data on study characteristics, participant characteristics, data collection characteristics, mental health outcomes, assessment tools, and associations found.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 17 studies involving 829 participants were included. Wearable devices and smartphones were used for passive data collection, most commonly incorporating accelerometers and GPS. Derived features covered activity, location and mobility, sleep, cardiac physiology, and device-use behavior. Depression and anxiety were the most frequently assessed mental health outcomes. Higher physical activity was generally associated with lower depression, anxiety, sadness, and psychological distress, whereas greater sedentary behavior and disrupted sleep or rest-activity rhythms were associated with higher psychological symptom levels.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Digital phenotyping shows potential to support remote mental health monitoring in patients with cancer. However, the current evidence remains limited and heterogeneous and is insufficient to support the routine clinical implementation of digital phenotyping. Future research should prioritize larger-scale, standardized, multicenter prospective studies.

items.title: Undiagnosed probable depression among middle-aged and older adults in China: a two-wave national comparison using CHARLS, 2011 and 2020.
items.authors: Wu Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Population based evidence comparing physician recognition of probable depression among Chinese middle aged and older adults across national survey waves remains limited.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were drawn from two waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 10,546 wave-specific observations from 8,754 unique respondents aged 45 years and older in 2011 and 2020. Probable depression was defined as a score of 10 or higher on the ten-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Undiagnosed probable depression was defined as a CES-D-10 score of 10 or higher without self-reported physician recognition of an emotional, nervous, or psychiatric problem. Survey-weighted logistic regression accounting for village/community-level clustering was used to examine the association between survey year and undiagnosed probable depression. Models adjusted for predisposing, enabling, and need-related characteristics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among observations with probable depression, the survey-weighted proportion without self-reported physician recognition was 98.23% (95% CI, 97.76%-98.60%) in 2011 and 95.61% (95% CI, 94.67%-96.39%) in 2020, corresponding to an absolute decrease of 2.62% points. After multivariable adjustment, the odds of lacking self-reported physician recognition were lower in 2020 than in 2011 (OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.32-0.64; P < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings indicate a substantial recognition gap among middle-aged and older adults in China and a modestly lower proportion of undiagnosed probable depression in 2020 than in 2011. This persistent recognition gap warrants continued attention in research and public health practice.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Digital Mental Health Interventions in Community-Based Care: Systematic Review.
items.authors: Farahain A, Firdaus MH, Daud F, Wahab S, Ahmad Marzuki M, Algumaei A, Mohd Yaacob N, Abdul Manaf MR.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mental health conditions are a leading cause of disability and economic burden worldwide. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) may widen access, but economic evidence from community mental health settings, including low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), has not been synthesized by perspective, time horizon, and comparator type.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to assess the cost-effectiveness of DMHIs delivered in community mental health settings.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This systematic review followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines and was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD420251141326). PubMed, Scopus, the Directory of Open Access Journals, and the Cochrane Library were searched for economic evaluations published from January 2010 to June 2025 involving adolescents (aged 10 years and older) through older adults with mental disorders. Two reviewers independently screened studies, and the quality was appraised using the Consensus on Health Economic Criteria (CHEC) list. Costs were standardized to 2025 US $, and findings were synthesized narratively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 2478 records identified, 20 economic evaluations were included: 16 randomized controlled trials, 3 decision-analytic models, and 1 uncontrolled single-arm study, conducted in high-income countries and LMICs (Kenya, Lebanon, China, and Southeast Europe). Depression (n=11, 55%) and anxiety (n=7, 35%) were the most frequent targets. Of 20 studies, 10 (50%) used a health care payer perspective only, 1 (5%) study used a societal perspective only, and 9 (45%) used both perspectives; time horizons ranged from 2 weeks to 10 years. Thirteen (65%) studies were cost-effective at the willingness-to-pay thresholds applied, and 4 (20%) were not; 3 (15%) did not state a threshold. Among the 16 studies reporting quality-adjusted life years, 4 (25%) were dominant (less costly and more effective), 11 (69%) were more costly and more effective, and 1 (6%) was less costly and less effective. The BlueIce smartphone app for self-harm and the NIDUS-Family (New Interventions for Independence in Dementia Studies) dementia intervention were dominant, whereas a societal perspective made some interventions cost-saving, such as Step-by-Step in Lebanon. Interventions that were not cost-effective included those evaluated in Germany, the United States, and Southeast Europe, and 1 psychosis trial with a high incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. Methodological quality was high in 15 (75%) studies, moderate in 4 (20%), and low in 1 (5%).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: DMHIs in community settings can offer good value for money, particularly guided internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy for depression and anxiety, and may be cost-saving from a societal perspective. The evidence is limited by short time horizons (often 12 months or less), waitlist and usual care comparators, and heterogeneous outcome measures. Future evaluations should use longer follow-ups, active comparators, and a common utility measure, ideally the EQ-5D questionnaire.

items.title: Network state transitions and connectivity alterations in attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and schizophrenia: a dynamic fMRI study.
items.authors: Agoalikum E, Klugah-Brown B, Wu H, Pacheco-Luna L, Carvalho AF, Stoyanov D, Maes M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) has become a powerful method for assessing time-varying brain dynamics in psychiatric disorders. However, it is unclear whether disruptions in network dynamics reflect disorder-specific dysfunction or shared transdiagnostic mechanisms. This work examined network state transitions and connectivity patterns in schizophrenia (SZ) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A sliding-window approach with k-means clustering identified four distinct, recurring dFNC states. Group differences in state-specific connectivity patterns, mean dwell time (MDT), fraction of time (FOT), and state transitions were evaluated along with correlations between dFNC temporal metrics and clinical symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Schizophrenia demonstrated increased MDT and FOT in states characterized by reduced network integration and greater segregation, compared to both ADHD and healthy control (HC). ADHD spent more time in states reflecting moderate connectivity patterns, suggesting altered but more flexible network dynamics relative to schizophrenia. Schizophrenia also showed increased network connectivity between cerebellar, control, and sensory networks, compared to ADHD. Clinically, higher MDT and FOT in state 2 were associated with physical anhedonia in SZ, while hyperactivity symptoms in SZ were associated with FOT in state 1.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings show that psychiatric disorders are characterized by instability in brain network dynamics, with both shared and disorder-specific features. Our results also align with frameworks emphasizing that psychopathology arises from graded disruptions in interacting neural systems rather than discrete diagnostic categories. These dFNC features may serve as potential biomarkers for symptom dimensions in schizophrenia and ADHD.

items.title: Reducing re-hospitalization in schizophrenia: real-world comparison of first- vs. second-generation long-acting injectable antipsychotics.
items.authors: de Filippis R, Aloi M, Pilieci AM, Carbone EA, Rania M, D'Onofrio E, Procopio C, Segura-Garcia C, De Fazio P.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics represent a valid and effective option in the pharmacological treatment of schizophrenia, but the choice between first- (FGA) and second-generation (SGA) LAIs is not always clear. We aimed to evaluate differences in reducing the frequency and duration of hospitalizations, clinical relapses and suicide attempts in patients suffering from schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs) by comparing introduction of FGA-LAIs vs. SGA-LAIs.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a mirror-image study with a three-year retrospective observation and follow-up time in patients with SSDs switching from oral antipsychotics to LAI formulations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The sample included 133 predominantly male (69.2%), middle-aged (mean 50.3 years), single, caucasian patients with a long-standing course of SSDs illness (20.1 years) and antipsychotic treatment (17.1 years). Initiation of LAI treatment was associated with a significant reduction in hospital admissions from 53.4% to 6.0% over three years, consistently observed across all patient subgroups and treatment conditions. The average duration of hospitalization decreased markedly, dropping from 14.26 days (± 29.1) to 1.35 days (± 8.09) after LAI start. Both FGA-LAIs and SGA-LAIs were associated with significant reductions in hospitalization days, relapses, and suicide attempts. No statistically significant differences in improvement were detected between the two groups in this cohort.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Treatment with LAI was associated with sustained medium- to long-term reductions in rehospitalizations, relapses, and suicide attempts in patients with SSD. However, because of the observational mirror-image design and the potential for residual confounding, the present findings should not be interpreted as establishing the comparative effectiveness of first- and second-generation LAIs. Treatment selection should therefore remain individualized, taking into account the overall clinical profile, tolerability, patient preferences, and clinician judgement.

items.title: Suicide attempt methods among patients referred for psychiatric evaluation at an advanced emergency and critical care medical center in Japan: associations with sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis: a single-center retrospective study.
items.authors: Ikehara M, Takada R, Okumura K, Nishi Y, Noriyama Y, Hamano Y, Mizui R, Fujimoto Y, Doi F, Fukui H, Honda Y, Araki S, Sunami Y, Yamanaka K, Urushitani S, Nishikawa N, Yamamuro K, Okada T.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicide attempts requiring emergency care provide a critical opportunity for psychiatric assessment and prevention. However, contemporary evidence from advanced emergency settings remains limited, particularly regarding how suicide attempt methods vary according to sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This single-center retrospective study included 344 patients who were transported to an advanced emergency and critical care medical center after suicide attempts and were subsequently referred for psychiatric evaluation between April 2014 and March 2024. Psychiatric diagnoses and suicide attempt methods were classified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision-based categories. The primary analyses examined sex-, age-, and diagnosis-specific patterns of suicide attempt methods. Secondary analyses compared high- and low-lethality attempts.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Drug overdose was the most common method and was more frequent among female patients. Substance use disorders were more frequent among male patients. Age-specific analyses showed that drug overdose was more frequent among patients aged < 20 years, whereas pesticide poisoning was more frequent among patients aged ≥ 65 years. Diagnosis-specific analyses showed that jumping from height was more frequent among patients with schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders. In secondary analyses, patients in the high-lethality group were older, although high- and low-lethality attempts were observed across diagnostic categories. Suicide attempt methods among patients referred for psychiatric evaluation after emergency transport varied according to sex, age, and psychiatric diagnosis.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings support post-attempt assessment in general hospital settings that integrates demographic and diagnostic context, the observed suicide attempt method, and medical severity rather than relying solely on categorized lethality.

items.title: The effects of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises on Post-Traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality in earthquake survivors.
items.authors: Kayaoğlu K, Ceviz R.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises on post-traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality in individuals affected by the February 6, 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye. While such interventions have shown promise in various trauma-exposed populations, their specific impact on earthquake survivors remains underexplored. The study sought to determine whether a structured, low-cost group-based intervention could improve psychological recovery and sleep quality in this vulnerable group.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A randomized controlled pre-test-post-test design was employed in this study. The population consisted of earthquake survivors residing in temporary shelters in Malatya, one of the provinces most severely affected by the February 6, 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye. A total of 203 earthquake survivors were assessed for eligibility; 90 participants were randomized equally into the intervention and control groups, and 84 completed the study and were included in the final analysis (42 in the intervention group and 42 in the control group). Data were collected using the sociodemographic form, the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Short Scale (PTSD-SS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The intervention group received six sessions of psychoeducation-supported breathing and relaxation exercises delivered in a group training format. No intervention was provided to the control group.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Following the intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in post-traumatic stress symptoms and sleep quality compared to the control group (p <.05). Specifically, the mean PTSD-SS score in the intervention group decreased by 5.45 points, and the mean PSQI score decreased by 3.88 points, indicating reduced post-traumatic stress symptoms and improved sleep quality.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Breathing and relaxation exercises supported by psychoeducation appear to be a low-cost and effective approach for reducing post-traumatic stress symptoms and improving sleep quality among individuals affected by disasters. The integration of such interventions into post-disaster psychosocial support programs may contribute to the mental health and overall well-being of earthquake survivors.

items.title: Substance Use, Internet Addiction, and Suicidality Among Sexual Minority and Heterosexual Chinese University Students: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Tang W, Wu S, Wang C, Xue S, Liu YH, Yang YY, Zhou L, Mu YF, Lan X, Hu T, Yang Q, Liu Q, Sun Z, Jin H, Xiao Y, Wen Y, Ahmad J, Cai J, Yin L, Liu B, Pan J, Ran MS.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicidality among university students poses a serious public health challenge, while addictive behaviors such as substance use and internet addiction are often overlooked, particularly in China. Sexual minority students may face additional risks; however, little is known about how suicidality and addictive behaviors differ by sexual orientation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A multicenter, cross-sectional online survey was conducted among students from 40 universities across China. Participants were categorized by self-reported sexual orientation as sexual minority (gay or lesbian) or heterosexual. Suicidal risk was assessed using questions on 12-month and lifetime suicidal ideation and attempts. Additional outcomes included depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), internet addiction (IAT-20), substance use, and screen time; for substance use, detailed information on type, frequency, and duration was collected.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Sexual minority students ( n  = 1178) had a higher prevalence of drug use and suicidality than heterosexual students ( n  = 21,426). Excessive screen time (>5 h/day) was associated with increased suicidal ideation in both groups and with suicide attempts among heterosexual students after adjustment for depressive symptoms. Internet addiction was directly associated with suicidal ideation only among heterosexual students. Drug use was associated with greater lifetime suicide attempts across groups, with risk increasing with frequency and duration of use. Ongoing alcohol use was associated with suicidality among sexual minority students, whereas frequent or prolonged alcohol and tobacco use was associated with suicide attempts among heterosexual students.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Addictive behaviors are strongly associated with suicidality among Chinese university students, with notable variation by sexual orientation. Sexual minority students reported a higher prevalence of drug use and suicidal ideation than their heterosexual peers. Targeted, culturally sensitive interventions that address both shared and group-specific factors are urgently needed.

items.title: Family environment and subjective wellbeing in adolescents: the mediating roles of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
items.authors: Li X, Li Q, Zhang C, Wang Q, Xu J, Liu S, Nie R, Zhao G.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescent depression and anxiety are major global health threats. As a core developmental microsystem, family environment strongly influences emotional states and subjective wellbeing (SWB). Few studies have explored whether affective symptoms mediate this association. Using data from treatment-seeking adolescents, we tested these mediating effects and gender differences.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In total, 1,284 adolescents recruited from a general hospital completed self-report questionnaires measuring family-environment indicators, including sibling status, parental marital quality (PMQ), family monthly income (FMI), family psychiatric history (FPH). Depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed using PHQ-9 and GAD-7, while the total score of Adolescent Students' Life Satisfaction Scale (ASLSS-T) and Family Life Satisfaction Subscale (ASLSS-FAM) served as SWB indicators.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Females reported higher PHQ-9/GAD-7 but lower ASLSS-T/FAM. PMQ correlated with lower PHQ-9/GAD-7 and higher ASLSS-T/FAM, whereas FPH correlated with more severe PHQ-9/GAD-7 and lower ASLSS-T/FAM. In full-sample mediation models, GAD-7 partially mediated PMQ-SWB and FPH-SWB associations; PHQ-9 fully mediated sibling status-ASLSS-T link and partially mediated pathways for PMQ and FPH. Descriptively among males, GAD-7 fully mediated the FPH-ASLSS-T association and both GAD-7 and PHQ-9 mediated FPH-related pathways. In females, GAD-7 showed no significant mediation, while only PHQ-9 partially mediated PMQ and FPH-ASLSS-T/FAM associations. Formal moderated-mediation analyses (PROCESS Model 59) revealed significant gender heterogeneity exclusively in FMI-to-SWB pathways via anxiety symptoms; most mediating pathways showed no significant gender differences.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study reveals that family environment is associated with SWB among treatment-seeking adolescents through the mediating effects of depressive and anxiety symptoms. These findings point to the possible utility of gender-differentiated, symptom-targeted family interventions in enhancing mental-health outcomes for at-risk treatment-seeking adolescents.

items.title: Bipolar Disorder Literacy: Protocol for a Scoping Review of Assessment Tools and Reported Literacy Levels.
items.authors: Mesbah R, Siu A, Keramatian K.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic and severe mental illness associated with substantial functional impairment, elevated suicide risk, and frequent diagnostic delays. Limited awareness and misconceptions about BD among the general public, caregivers, and health professionals contribute to underrecognition and misdiagnosis. Although mental health literacy is known to facilitate early recognition and appropriate help-seeking, BD-specific literacy and its measurement remain poorly understood. No synthesis currently exists of instruments used to assess BD literacy, or of reported literacy levels across populations.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This scoping review aims to (1) identify and map instruments used to measure BD literacy across different populations and contexts and (2) synthesize reported levels of BD literacy as assessed by these instruments.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This scoping review will follow the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. We will search MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, and CINAHL for peer-reviewed primary studies. Included studies will report on tools measuring one or more components of BD literacy across populations and settings. Two independent reviewers will screen studies and extract data using a standardized charting form developed in accordance with the population, concept, and context framework and the review objectives. Findings will be synthesized descriptively and organized by population group.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The review was registered with the Open Science Framework (digital object identifier: 10.17605/OSF.IO/9E3MF). The literature search and study selection process were completed in July 2026, resulting in the inclusion of 111 studies. Data charting and evidence synthesis were completed in September 2026. Preparation of the completed scoping review manuscript is expected to be finalized by December 2026. Findings from the evidence synthesis are not presented in this protocol.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This review will be the first to comprehensively map BD literacy instruments and synthesize evidence on measured literacy levels. The findings will inform instrument selection; highlight gaps in assessment and knowledge; and guide future research, validation efforts, and targeted educational interventions.

items.title: Psychometric Properties and Predictive Performance of the Czech Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale for Mental Health Outcomes: Validation and Multivariable Modeling Study in an Adult Convenience Sample.
items.authors: Buchta O, Buchtova M, Novak L, Bakker M, Malinakova K, Helvich J, Tavel P.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Problematic social media use (PSMU) is linked to depression, anxiety, and loneliness, requiring valid measurement tools. The Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) is the most widely used PSMU measure internationally, but has not been validated in Czech adults.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to (1) validate the Czech BSMAS by evaluating structural validity, internal consistency, measurement invariance, and construct validity, and comparing latent-factor and network representations; and (2) evaluate, in a multivariable prediction-modeling framework with an independent replication sample, whether item-level BSMAS scores predict depression, anxiety, and loneliness better than the conventional sum score.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Two independent nonprobability convenience samples of Czech adults were recruited online via snowball sampling (primary: N=3297; replication: N=514). Structural validity was assessed with confirmatory factor analysis; internal consistency with α and ω. Measurement invariance across gender (configural, metric, and scalar) and differential item functioning across age were assessed. Construct validity was explored through Spearman correlations with depression, anxiety, and loneliness (total, emotional, and social). Latent and network models were compared using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC). For prediction, 5 algorithms compared the BSMAS sum score with the 6 individual items as predictors, using repeated 10-fold cross-validation; performance was quantified with out-of-sample R ^2 and root-mean-square error. The item-level comparison was additionally evaluated with models fixed in the primary sample and applied unchanged to the replication sample, and with sociodemographic characteristics held constant (registered on Open Science Framework: v9emk).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A one-factor model fit well ( χ ^2_9=101.5, P <.001; comparative fit index [CFI]=0.993; root-mean-square error of approximation [RMSEA]=0.056) and reproduced in the replication sample. Internal consistency was high (α=0.87; ω =0.87). Scalar invariance across gender was supported; 2 of 6 items showed differential item functioning across age. Correlations were moderate with depression (ρ=0.31-0.38) and anxiety (ρ=0.32-0.45), small with emotional loneliness (ρ=0.28-0.29), and negligible to small with social loneliness (ρ=0.03-0.16). The latent model was more parsimonious than the network model (ΔBIC=-59.32). Item-level representation modestly outperformed the sum score for depression ( R ²=0.15 vs 0.10) and anxiety ( R ²=0.16 vs 0.11). This advantage was reproduced in the replication sample, held with models fixed in the primary sample (Δ R ²=0.069, 90% CI 0.040-0.100, and 0.067, 90% CI 0.043-0.093) and after sociodemographic adjustment, and was not accounted for by weighting items by their standardized factor loadings. More flexible algorithms did not outperform linear regression. Loneliness, especially its social dimension, was poorly predicted by BSMAS scores.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In these samples, the Czech BSMAS showed a predominantly unidimensional structure and high internal consistency, with scalar invariance across gender but age-related differential item functioning in 2 items. Item-level scoring offered a small, reproducible predictive advantage for depression and anxiety, although absolute predictive performance was low. Replication in representative samples is needed before population-level or clinical application.

items.title: Oral health-related behaviors and mental health among children of migrant workers in China.
items.authors: Zhou H, Wu H, Ge X, Li Y, Sun H, Zhang W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This study aims to investigate differences in oral health-related behaviors of local children and children whose parents were rural-to-urban migrant workers, and explore the relationship between oral health-related behaviors and mental health.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A valid sample of 1331 students from 3 primary schools in Hangzhou was included. Participants were questioned about the frequency of tooth brushing, and sugary drinking consumption. A Chinese language Mental Health Test (MHT) scale was also used to assess children's mental health. Differences between the groups were analyzed using Chi-square and independent t-test. Logistic regressions were performed to evaluate the association between oral health-related behaviors and mental health.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among the 1199 students who completed the survey, 575(47.8%) were children of migrant workers (CMW). They brushed their teeth less (p = 0.003) and had higher scores of MHT (p = 0.007) than local children. Logistic regression revealed that CMW with mental health problems were more likely to brush their teeth less than twice per day (OR = 1.95, p < 0.01), and consume soft drinks once or more per day (OR = 1.73, p < 0.05). Tooth brushing was associated with Loneliness tendency(p = 0.001),Sensitiveness tendency(p = 0.001),Body anxiety(p = 0.001),Impulsive tendency(p < 0.001) of MHT, whereas soft drink consumption was associated with Learning anxiety(p = 0.003), Personal anxiety(p = 0.007), and Sensitiveness tendency(p = 0.032).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: CMW has a lower frequency of brushing teeth and a higher risk of mental health problems than local children. Their oral health-related behaviors were associated with their mental health scores. Comprehensive intervention strategies are warranted, including the promotion of healthy beverage policies in schools, the integration of oral and mental health assessments with behavioral interventions, and the provision of targeted support for vulnerable groups.

items.title: Sleep disturbances in children with cystic fibrosis on highly effective modulator therapy referred for polysomnography.
items.authors: Shakkottai A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Sleep disturbances are increasingly recognized in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), including those on highly effective modulator therapy (HEMT), but polysomnographic data remain limited and the factors associated with these disturbances are poorly understood.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Single-center retrospective review of polysomnographic data from 2015 to 2025 in children with CF to evaluate associations between sleep outcomes and non-pulmonary comorbidities known to affect sleep including iron deficiency, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety/depression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Sixty children with CF underwent polysomnography (mean age 8.8 ± 4.6 years) with 58% receiving HEMTs for an average of 2.1 ± 1.4 years. Sleep complaints were common overall: snoring (85%), insomnia symptoms (71%), restless sleep (71%), hypersomnolence (29%). Although snoring was more prevalent in the non-HEMT group (p = 0.008), children on HEMTs had 4.7-fold higher odds of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), independent of age, nutritional status, adenoid/tonsillar hypertrophy, and dependence on nocturnal feeds (p = 0.037). They also had poorer sleep efficiency (p = 0.028) and more prolonged sleep-onset latency (p = 0.038) as compared to children not on modulators, even after accounting for age differences between the groups. Adenoid/tonsillar hypertrophy and nocturnal feeding both emerged as being significant predictors of OSA, independent of age, nutritional status, and HEMT use (p < 0.05). Iron deficiency, present in 70% regardless of HEMT use, was associated with restless sleep (p = 0.0002) and insomnia symptoms (p = 0.037). ADHD and anxiety/depression, each present in approximately 22% independent of HEMT, were also associated with multiple subjective and objective markers of disturbed sleep.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Iron deficiency, neurodevelopmental/mental health comorbidities appear to be common among children with CF undergoing polysomnography and were associated with both subjective sleep complaints and objective polysomnographic abnormalities. Children receiving HEMTs had greater odds of OSA and differences in sleep architecture compared with those not receiving modulators. Nocturnal feedings also appear to adversely influence sleep in children with CF, independent of HEMT use. These findings highlight the importance of considering non-pulmonary comorbidities when evaluating sleep disturbances in pediatric CF and support the need for prospective longitudinal studies to better characterize these associations.

Iron deficiency, neurodevelopmental/mental health comorbidities appear to be common among children with CF undergoing polysomnography and were associated with both subjective sleep complaints and objective polysomnographic abnormalities. Children receiving HEMTs had greater odds of OSA and differences in sleep architecture compared with those not receiving modulators. Nocturnal feedings also appear to adversely influence sleep in children with CF, independent of HEMT use. These findings highlight the importance of considering non-pulmonary comorbidities when evaluating sleep disturbances in pediatric CF and support the need for prospective longitudinal studies to better characterize these associations.

items.title: Exploring how the surge of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnoses has influenced the lives of young adults diagnosed with ADHD in childhood - a qualitative study.
items.authors: Carlsson C, Jarbin H, Larsson I.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In recent years, a drastic surge in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder diagnoses has occurred. In the wake of this, more persons with only mild to moderate impairment of function and low levels of comorbidities receive a diagnosis. The balance between benefits and risks may be less obvious in these cases. The aim of this study was to explore the influence of receiving an ADHD diagnosis in childhood on the lives of young adults.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study had a qualitative design, with interviews conducted in March 2026. Seventeen young adults who in early school years were diagnosed with "uncomplicated" (i.e., without comorbidities or social burden) ADHD with mild to moderate impairment of function were interviewed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The results revealed that an early diagnosis of ADHD contributed to better self-understanding and promoted understanding from others. It also provided access to important support interventions, such as adaptations and medication. For some, the diagnosis came with a feeling of being different, whereas for others, the diagnosis helped them gain a sense of community with others.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings suggest that, in this group of young adults, receiving an ADHD diagnosis in childhood was mainly described as supportive, although experiences varied. The diagnosis appeared to provide a foundation for managing life with ADHD while also involving some challenging experiences. The voices of these young adults should not dissuade us from diagnosing ADHD in children with milder presentations of ADHD.

items.title: Adherence to the Mediterranean dietary pattern and mental health outcomes in Hong Kong adults: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Ho FY, Wong VW, Hui BP, O'Neil A, Marx W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adherence to the Mediterranean dietary pattern (MDP) has been associated with lower depressive, anxiety, and insomnia symptoms, yet associations with stress, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and functional impairment, as well as those of individual MDP components, remain underexplored in Chinese adults.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional survey of 1,355 Hong Kong adults examined associations between MDP adherence and depressive, anxiety, and insomnia symptoms, perceived stress, HRQoL, and functional impairment. Hierarchical linear regression compared moderate-to-high with low MDP adherence, adjusting for sociodemographic and lifestyle covariates. Analyses of individual dietary components were exploratory.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Compared with low adherence, moderate-to-high MDP adherence was associated with lower depressive (B = -0.79, 95% CI -1.34 to -0.25), anxiety (B = -0.71, 95% CI -1.25 to -0.17), and insomnia symptoms (B = -0.66, 95% CI -1.29 to -0.03), and perceived stress (B = -1.50, 95% CI -2.47 to -0.54), and better HRQoL (B = 0.03, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.04), but not functional impairment. Exploratory analyses indicated that higher vegetable consumption was associated with lower anxiety and insomnia symptoms and better HRQoL, whereas lower sweetened drink, commercial sweets and pastries, and butter, margarine, or cream consumption with lower insomnia symptoms, perceived stress, and functional impairment, respectively. No component was significantly associated with depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Higher MDP adherence was associated with more favorable mental health outcomes and better HRQoL. Findings may inform culturally informed dietary intervention research aimed at evaluating potential effects on mental health. The non-probability sample and cross-sectional design limit generalizability and preclude causal inference.

items.title: Preoperative depression or anxiety and late new-onset atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery: an observational cohort study.
items.authors: Stenman M, Jackson V, Särnholm J, Pettersson L, Sartipy U, Nielsen SJ.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: The aim was to study the association between preoperative depression or anxiety and incidence of late new-onset atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

sections.heading: Methods and results
sections.text: Data from five national registers including 44 338 patients who underwent primary cardiac surgery in Sweden between 2006 and 2020 were used, excluding those with a prior diagnosis of atrial fibrillation. Follow-up for atrial fibrillation occurred >30 days after surgery. Cox regression models were used to estimate the association between preoperative depression or anxiety and new late-onset atrial fibrillation in the total study population and according to sex and age categories. In total, 1037 (12%) of the patients with preoperative depression or anxiety, and 5036 (14%) of those without, developed late new-onset atrial fibrillation following cardiac surgery. Patients with depression or anxiety had an increased risk of developing atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.09; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-1.17]. Sex-specific analysis showed that men with depression or anxiety had an increased risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation (aHR 1.14; 95% CI 1.05-1.25), whereas this increased risk was not observed in women (aHR 1.00; 95% CI 0.89-1.13).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Patients with preoperative depression or anxiety undergoing primary cardiac surgery had an increased risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation. This association was predominantly observed in men under 75 years of age. Routine screening for depression and anxiety can identify patients at risk. Comprehensive care, including mental health support, lifestyle changes, and medication management, may reduce the risk of late new-onset atrial fibrillation.

items.title: Caught in the moment: Do momentary dissociative aspects differentiate Maladaptive daydreaming from ADHD?
items.authors: Theodor-Katz N, Soffer-Dudek N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Maladaptive daydreaming (MD) is a clinical condition of recurring, and prolonged episodes of daydreaming, resulting in distress and impaired functioning. It is often considered a dissociative syndrome of pathological "absorption and imaginative involvement" motivated by escapism. However, it shares the adverse outcome of attention impairment with Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Despite MD being characterized by immersive daydreaming whereas ADHD by mind wandering, both conditions hinder attention via shifting attention inwards at the expense of actively pursuing personal goals. While previous studies supported the separateness of the conditions, they have not compared moment-to-moment dynamics. The present study aimed to explore whether momentary elevations in the motivation to daydream and in immersive daydreaming are accompanied by heightened dissociative characteristics (absorption and detachment), and whether this dynamic distinguishes MD from ADHD.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using experience sampling, four groups of: ADHD (n = 35), MD (n = 48), ADHD + MD (n = 33), and Controls (n = 35), diagnosed through a clinical interview, rated their daydreaming and dissociation levels four times a day across five days. Each group was predominantly female, and the MD groups were significantly younger than the non-MD groups (ADHD 68.57%, M_age = 39.9, MD 66.66%, M_age = 29.4, ADHD + MD 81.81%, M_age = 30.8, Control 60%, M_age = 37.1).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Immersive daydreaming and the desire to daydream fluctuated in tandem with increased dissociation (both absorption and detachment). Moreover, an expected interaction effect emerged, whereby the coupling of immersive daydreaming with dissociation was more pronounced in MD compared to ADHD. When focusing on the desire to daydream, and/or when comparing to controls, the interaction effects were limited to absorption and not detachment.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The present study supports the notion that MD momentary dynamics are distinguished from ADHD distractibility.

items.title: Psychometric properties, construct validity and invariance across sexes of the fear of COVID-19 scale in Brazilian high-school adolescents.
items.authors: de Almeida AA, Teixeira-Silva AC, Oliveira MA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The outbreak of COVID-19 precipitated not only a global public health emergency but also an unprecedented psychological crisis. Consequently, there has been a documented surge in negative psychiatric outcomes, with fear, depression and anxiety emerging as the most salient psychological responses to the pandemic. Regarding fear, valid instruments for assessing this feeling are scarce among Brazilian adolescents.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To verify the psychometric properties and biological sex invariance of Brazilian version of Fear of COVID-19 Scale in a sample of Brazilian adolescents girls and boys.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 543 Brazilian adolescents were included in this study. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) with a Diagonally Weighted Least Squares estimator was used to verify the psychometric properties of the Fear of COVID-19 Scale. To evaluate the concurrent and criterion validities Spearman's correlations with the DASS-21 and social distancing index were stablished.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The CFA supported the unidimensional structure and internal consistency (ω = 0.901) of the FCV-19s in our sample. Multigroup CFA showed that FCV-19s was fully invariant across biological sex. The factorial score of the Fear of COVID-19 Scale demonstrated significant positive correlations with depression (r_s = 0.236), anxiety (r_s = 0.296), and stress (r_s = 0.312) subscales and total DASS-21 scores (r_s = 0.302), thereby supporting its concurrent validity. Furthermore, preliminary construct validity based on associations with external variables was established through a significant positive association with the social distancing index (r_s = 0.208).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The FCV-19s is a reliable psychometric instrument for assessing the fear of COVID-19 in Brazilian adolescents, within findings from the validity and reliability analyses indicating that the scale has a stable one-factor structure.

items.title: Polygenic architecture of childhood emotional and behavioral problems in East Asian youth: a multivariate genome-wide study.
items.authors: Lai HH, Lo CY, Cheng YC, Kuo PH.
items.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Emotional and behavioral problems in childhood, commonly classified as internalizing and externalizing symptoms, represent early manifestations of vulnerability to later psychiatric disorders. However, their genetic architecture remains largely characterized in European populations, with limited evidence from East Asian cohorts.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted the first multivariate genome-wide association study of 1522 school-aged children from Taiwan. Using parent-reported Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) scores and approximately 6 million SNPs, we jointly assess genetic associations across internalizing, externalizing, and total problem dimensions. Gene-based and tissue enrichment analyses were performed to examine biological relevance. To index shared polygenic liability across psychiatric disorders, we constructed a meta-polygenic risk score (metaPRS) via elastic-net regression integrating risk profiles from a number of major psychiatric conditions and examined its association with symptom dimensions and suicidal behaviors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A few genome-wide significant loci were identified (p < 5 × 10⁻⁸), including variants mapping to genes previously implicated in mood and neurodevelopmental pathways (e.g., BCL9, ADARB2, FGGY). Tissue enrichment analyses highlighted expression patterns in brain regions central to emotion regulation, including the anterior cingulate cortex, hypothalamus, and cerebellum, as well as peripheral cardiac and intestinal tissues. The metaPRS accounted for modest but significant variance (0.86-1.18%) in internalizing and externalizing symptoms, and significantly predicted increased suicidal ideation, highlighting the early emergence of transdiagnostic polygenic vulnerability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings provide an initial genomic characterization of childhood emotional and behavioral problems in East Asian youth and support the presence of shared polygenic liability across early psychopathology. They also highlight the value of ancestry-diverse and multivariate approaches in developmental psychiatric genetics. Given the modest sample size, the identified loci should be considered preliminary and require independent replication. With validation in larger cohorts, these findings may inform future research on risk stratification and precision mental health across populations.

items.title: Psychiatric and Neuropsychiatric Phenotypes in Alcohol-Related Liver Disease: Clinical and Biochemical Associations.
items.authors: Sarpe AM, Onisor C, Niculet E, Anghel L, Drima EP.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) is frequently accompanied by psychiatric and neuropsychiatric manifestations that contribute to disease complexity. This hospital-based observational study aimed to characterize psychiatric and neuropsychiatric comorbidity patterns in a single-center series of 50 patients with ALD and to explore their associations with demographic characteristics and biochemical profiles, including serum immunoglobulin A (IgA) and immunoglobulin G (IgG).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this observational study, 50 consecutively hospitalized patients with ALD were evaluated. Neuropsychiatric manifestations-namely hepatic encephalopathy (HE, assessed clinically and graded using West Haven criteria), anxiety-depressive manifestations, delirium tremens, alcohol-related psychosis, and insomnia-were recorded based on clinical evaluation without standardized psychometric rating scales. Demographic characteristics and biochemical parameters (IgA, IgG, liver enzymes, bilirubin, albumin, INR, hemoglobin, MCV, and platelets) were compared between groups using non-parametric tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with HE.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: HE was present in 60% of patients, anxiety-depressive manifestations in 54.0%, insomnia in 50.0%, alcoholic psychosis in 22%, and delirium tremens in 16.0%. Patients with HE exhibited significantly higher IgA (7.09 ± 2.33 vs. 4.94 ± 2.39 g/L, p = 0.003) and IgG concentrations (16.83 ± 3.68 vs. 13.72 ± 4.55 g/L, p = 0.029), alongside lower hemoglobin levels ( p = 0.025). In multivariable analysis, age 51-70 years (OR = 11.882, 95% CI: 2.268-62.244, p = 0.003) and higher IgG concentrations (OR = 1.288 per g/L, 95% CI: 1.035-1.603, p = 0.023) remained independently associated with HE.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Psychiatric and neuropsychiatric comorbidities are frequent in hospitalized patients with ALD. Given the observational design, lack of standardized psychometric scales, and small sample size, these exploratory findings-particularly the immunological associations-require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

items.title: Perinatal Psychosocial Profiles and Offspring Longitudinal Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Latent Analysis Approach.
items.authors: Roumeliotaki T, Koutra K, Chatzi L, Kritsotakis G, Benetou V, Symvoulakis EK.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Early-life exposures, including maternal psychosocial profile, can shape an individual's lifelong development. There is growing interest in the effects of prenatal exposures on cardiometabolic health through childhood. The present study used latent profile analysis to identify psychosocial profiles among pregnant women by examining the co-occurrence of personality traits, anxiety, depression, and social capital and compared them with offspring health outcomes.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Latent analysis identified three distinct psychosocial profiles for 638 participants from the Rhea cohort, following the use of multiple imputation techniques, based on a total analytic sample of 1340 participants.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The "Normative" profile (51.2%) had near-zero scores across all standardised psychosocial indicators, representing the baseline group. The "Resilient-Socially Resourced" profile (28.7%) was characterised by low anxiety, neuroticism, and prenatal depression, and high extraversion and social engagement. The "Psychosocially Vulnerable" profile (20.1%) exhibited high anxiety, neuroticism, and prenatal depression, with low extraversion and social connectedness. Associations between maternal psychosocial profiles and offspring cardiometabolic outcomes at ages 4, 7, and 11 years were generally weak and inconsistent. On the contrary, latent socioeconomic classes showed larger effects. Children of "Younger and socioeconomically vulnerable individuals" showed a three-fold higher risk of hypertension at age 4, compared to those from "Professional and well-resourced families".

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Findings suggest that although distinct maternal psychosocial profiles can be identified, they may have limited influence on offspring cardiometabolic risk through mid-childhood. Further research is needed to clarify how psychosocial and socioeconomic exposures interact across the life course and influence offspring health trajectories.

items.title: Set-Level Cross-Tissue and Longitudinal Transportability of Discovery-Defined DNA Methylation Regions from Social Anxiety Disorder: A Cross-Cohort Analysis.
items.authors: Su Y.

sections.text: Background: Epigenome-wide association studies have reported candidate DNA methylation signals for anxiety disorders, but their stability across tissues and developmental periods remains uncertain. This study evaluated locus-specific and set-level transportability of adult whole-blood methylation signals associated with social anxiety disorder to longitudinal saliva measurements from a youth cohort characterized by a broader anxiety-related phenotype. Methods: The discovery cohort comprised 143 adults with social anxiety disorder or control status profiled using the Illumina Methylation EPIC array. The external cohort comprised 94 HumanMethylation450 saliva samples from 47 participants assessed in 2008 and 2013. Discovery analyses included CpG-wise and regional association testing, co-methylation analysis, and nested elastic-net modelling. A locked set of discovery differentially methylated regions (DMRs) was evaluated using wave-specific regional tests, directional concordance, covariate-adjusted permutation tests, cross-cohort effect correlations, matched genomic windows, and participant-blocked longitudinal models. Results: No individual CpG reached false-discovery-rate significance, whereas 130 DMRs met the harmonic-mean false-discovery-rate criterion. Ninety-seven DMRs contained at least two eligible saliva probes. In 2008, 61/97 regions were directionally concordant with discovery (62.9%; exact p = 0.0072; adjusted p = 0.014). Covariate-adjusted permutation tests, discovery-external effect correlations, and matched-window analyses also supported transportability of the DMR set. No corresponding set-level evidence was detected in 2013, and no individual external DMR survived multiple-testing correction at either wave. The locked 20-CpG classifier yielded a mean nested-cross-validation AUC of 0.596 and external AUCs of 0.735 and 0.455 in 2008 and 2013, respectively. Conclusions: Discovery-defined blood DNA methylation regions associated with adult social anxiety disorder showed set-level transportability to the earlier saliva assessment of a broader anxiety-related phenotype, without corrected locus-specific replication. This evidence was not sustained at follow-up, supporting assessment-specific ensemble transportability rather than a stable or clinically validated methylation biomarker.

items.title: Virtual reality exposure therapy for anxiety and trauma-related disorders: clinical evidence, behavioral sensing, and implementation priorities.
items.authors: Devaraj G, Srinivasan K.

sections.text: Virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) provides a controlled environment for delivering exposure to feared cues. Evidence supports benefit over inactive controls for selected specific phobias and social-anxiety presentations, but nonsignificant differences from active treatment do not establish equivalence. This critical narrative review integrates systematic reviews, representative randomized trials, mechanistic studies, and measurement and implementation frameworks. We distinguish diagnosed social anxiety disorder from performance-focused and symptom-selected samples, and exposure-based treatment from VR distraction or relaxation. PTSD findings require particular caution because military cohorts, trauma cues, and treatment histories may not represent civilian clinical populations. Behavioral and physiological signals are examined at four levels: technical capture, experimental association, clinical validity, and incremental clinical utility. Feasible recording and associations with arousal or attention do not establish that a signal measures therapeutic learning or improves treatment decisions. We propose a clinician-governed precision VRET loop as a conceptual framework requiring prospective evaluation, rather than a clinically validated adaptive intervention. Research priorities include appropriately designed comparative trials, explicit diagnostic characterization, standardized intervention and hardware reporting, purpose-specific measurement validation, systematic harms assessment, longer follow-up, and implementation and economic evaluation. VRET should be evaluated as a defined exposure intervention for a specified population and care setting, with patient choice and accountable clinical oversight.

items.title: Associations between insomnia and suicidal ideation in depressed adolescents: the mediating effect of cognitive symptoms and sex differences.
items.authors: Liu Y, Liu L, Tang P, Wang J, Chen C, Liu Z, Geng F, Mo D, Luo X, Wen X, Xia L, Liu H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Among adolescents diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD), suicidal ideation (SI) may be closely linked to cognitive symptoms and insomnia. However, the potential pathways connecting these three factors remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the mediating role of cognitive symptoms between insomnia and SI, and to further examine whether this mediating pathway differs by sex.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2021 to September 2023, recruiting 332 adolescents diagnosed with MDD and 123 healthy controls (HCs). To assess depression severity, cognitive symptoms, insomnia, and suicidal ideation (SI), we administered the Clinical Global Impression - Severity Scale (CGI-S), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-24 (HAMD-24), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), and Positive and Negative Suicide Ideation inventory (PANSI), respectively. The PROCESS macro (Model 4) for SPSS was employed to perform mediation analysis, examining whether cognitive symptoms mediated the relationship between insomnia and SI.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: SI was significantly more prevalent among adolescents with MDD than among their healthy counterparts. Within the MDD group, PANSI scores were negatively correlated with sex, age, and age of onset, but positively correlated with CGI-S, ISI, and HAMD-Cog scores (all p  < 0.001). These correlations were more pronounced among female patients. Mediation analysis demonstrated that cognitive symptoms, significantly mediated the relationship between insomnia severity (ISI) and suicidal ideation (PANSI). In the overall sample, the total effect, direct effect, and indirect effect values were 0.657 (95% CI: 0.452 - 0.863), 0.463 (95% CI: 0.279 - 0.647), and 0.195 (95% CI: 0.096 - 0.303), respectively. A sex-stratified analysis revealed a significant mediation effect among female patients, with total, direct, and indirect effect values of 0.734 (95% CI: 0.502 - 0.966), 0.539 (95% CI: 0.326 - 0.752), and 0.195 (95% CI: 0.088 - 0.315), respectively. Conversely, in male patients, neither the total nor the direct effects were statistically significant (confidence intervals included zero), and the indirect effect also lacked statistical significance (effect size: 0.132, 95% CI: -0.064 - 0.345), indicating that the mediating role of cognitive symptoms was not supported in this subgroup.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Adolescents with MDD exhibit elevated levels of SI, which is significantly associated with both cognitive symptoms and insomnia, particularly among females. Furthermore, cognitive symptoms could serve as a mediating factor in the link between insomnia and SI. This indirect effect was statistically significant in female patients, while results for male patients were inconclusive due to limited sample size. Consequently, in clinical practice, it is essential to understand the interconnected pathways linking insomnia, cognitive symptoms, and SI, with close attention to sex differences in the underlying mechanisms. This approach is crucial for enabling more precise risk assessment and targeted intervention.

items.title: Associations of remnant cholesterol with mental disorders: findings from retrospective cohort and Mendelian randomization analyses.
items.authors: Ouyang X, Fu Q, Liu S, Luo R, Zhou E, Huang J, Jiang L, Xu Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Remnant cholesterol (RC) is an independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The relationship between RC and mental disorders is not clear. This study sets out to evaluate associations between RC and mental disorders via retrospective cohort and bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) approaches.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study used data on anxiety and depression from NHANES and the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University. Correlation analysis, restricted cubic splines, logistic regression, and stratified regression were employed to examine the associations between RC and these mental health conditions. Bidirectional MR analyses evaluated RC and 20 mental disorders. Instruments were selected at P < 5 × 10^-6 for the main analysis, with a complementary sensitivity analysis using genome-wide significant instruments (P < 5 × 10^-8). The Bonferroni threshold for 40 directional tests was P < 0.00125.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Retrospective analysis of clinical EHR showed no association between RC and depression; instead, RC was significantly negatively correlated with anxiety. The NHANES-based retrospective analysis revealed no association between RC levels and either anxiety or depression. In the MR analysis, genetically predicted RC was positively associated with LBD (OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19-1.77; P = 0.0002) and APOE4-positive LBD (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.64-4.28; P = 0.000073), and both associations remained below the Bonferroni threshold. The corresponding estimates remained directionally consistent in the genome-wide-significance sensitivity analysis.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study provides complementary evidence from clinical, population-based, and genetic analyses regarding the relationship between RC and mental disorders. Lower RC was associated with anxiety in the hospital cohort, while genetically predicted RC was positively associated with LBD-related outcomes. Further investigation in independent populations is warranted.

items.title: Smart psychological service platform usage frequency and depressive symptoms among university students: a chain mediation model involving psychological capital and self-compassion.
items.authors: Ran H, Wang H, Yao L, Zhu E.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examined the associations between the usage frequency of Smart Psychological Service Platforms (SPSPs) and depressive symptoms among university students, as well as the chain mediation of psychological capital and self-compassion in this association.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 1,082 university students. The mediating roles of psychological capital and self-compassion, including their sequential indirect association, were examined.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: SPSP usage frequency was significantly and negatively associated with depressive symptoms among university students. Both psychological capital and self-compassion served as independent mediators in this association. A significant sequential indirect effect was also observed, linking SPSP usage frequency to depressive symptoms through psychological capital and subsequently self-compassion. The pathway "usage frequency → psychological capital → depressive symptoms" showed the largest indirect effect, followed by the chain pathway "usage frequency → psychological capital → self-compassion → depressive symptoms," whereas the pathway "usage frequency → self-compassion → depressive symptoms" was comparatively weaker.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The findings suggest that external digital mental health resources may be associated with internal positive psychological strengths, extending COR theory into the field of digital health. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed indirect associations should not be interpreted as evidence of causal mechanisms. These findings provide provisional, hypothesis-generating evidence that may inform universities' efforts to optimise smart mental health service platforms, refine promotion strategies, and develop targeted digital interventions. Further longitudinal and experimental research is needed to establish causal relationships and evaluate these implications.

items.title: English immersive game participation and attention, emotional health, and cognitive function in children: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Wu J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Screen exposure is an important issue for children's health. The existing research pays more attention to the duration of use, but not to the content type and immersion experience. English immersion game integrates language learning and game mechanism, which belongs to educational digital behavior. This study analyzes the daily English game duration, immersion and English integration of children aged 6-14, and their relationships with attention, working memory, executive function and emotional behavior.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 215 children. Based on the parents' questionnaire, the data of English game participation were obtained: daily duration, 1-5 immersion self-evaluation, and English integration. The outcome includes all kinds of attention, working memory, executive function, emotion and ADHD symptoms. Multivariate linear regression controls total screen time, sleep, physical activity, age, gender and family SES. CPT, Flanker and Corsi were the main outcomes, and after Bonferroni correction, the four executive function and behavior indicators were set as exploratory outcomes, which were not corrected.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: English game time is positively correlated with selective attention ( β  = 0.218, p  = 0.001). It is significantly different from the primary analysis of working memory, and its effect size fell below the minimum-detectable-effect threshold following Bonferroni correction. Immersion self-rating is positively correlated with multiple attention and working memory, and negatively correlated with emotional symptoms. The degree of English integration is positively correlated with cognitive indicators and negatively correlated with emotional symptoms; After excluding the pure-English-immersion subgroup, the association with selective attention and inhibition control is no longer significant, and it is regarded as descriptive association. Daily screen time was negatively correlated with cognitive ability, and positively correlated with mood and ADHD symptoms (all p  < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Different dimensions of English immersion games are related to children's cognitive and emotional outcomes. In addition to the duration of use, the integration of game English is as important as the immersion experience. The results can provide reference for family digital activity selection, children's screen behavior norms and campus digital education intervention, which still needs to be verified by longitudinal research.

items.title: Beyond Pills: Moving Towards the Use of Virtual Bikes and Virtual Reality Headsets to Treat Depression in Elderly People with Cognitive Impairments in Care Homes.
items.authors: Machot-Isaac D, Lefèvre C, Kabuth B, Clément-Ruillet C.

sections.text: Nowadays, the management of depressive disorders in older people is a major public health issue. Whilst pharmacological treatment is still prescribed in all cases, the need to provide accessible psychotherapy to residents of care homes for older people with cognitive impairments presents an additional challenge. This narrative review of the literature assesses how virtual exercise bikes and virtual reality headsets can be integrated into structured non-pharmacological care pathways. Both tools are already widely used in care homes. The former is used for functional rehabilitation and the latter for the management of pain or anxiety. Their acceptability and the existing infrastructure make them realistic candidates for repurposing towards mental health care, particularly for the management of depression in older people with neurocognitive disorders. Indeed, studies conducted amongst the general elderly population have demonstrated the effectiveness of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) in combating depressive disorders and, more specifically, 'next-generation' CBT approaches that draw on digital technologies and virtual reality. These have demonstrated greater acceptability and yielded very promising results in recent years. However, the integration of these therapies into long-term care settings faces numerous challenges: acquisition and maintenance costs, a lack of infrastructure, the need to train already overburdened staff, and the absence of validated care protocols. This review examines the feasibility, safety and clinical value of using these readily accessible tools to treat depression in older people in care homes with cognitive impairment. However, it also emphasises the importance of conducting research that will lead to the development of evaluated, standardised and validated care protocols.

items.title: Self-Forgiveness as a Potential Protective Factor for Mental Health and Well-Being in Older Adults: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: de Jesús Araujo G, López J, Pérez Rojo G.

sections.text: Depression, chronic guilt, regret, and suicidal ideation are common and often under-recognised sources of suffering in later life, yet geriatric care has traditionally focused on risk and deficit rather than on modifiable psychological strengths. Self-forgiveness, the process of replacing persistent guilt, shame, and self-condemnation after a perceived wrongdoing with an accepting, responsible, and self-compassionate stance toward oneself, has been proposed as one such strength, but it is understudied in older adults and rarely considered in clinical practice. This narrative review synthesises the empirical evidence on self-forgiveness and mental-health, well-being, and physical-health outcomes in adults aged 60 and over, and considers its implications for geriatric care. After briefly defining self-forgiveness, we introduce the distinctions between genuine and pseudo self-forgiveness and between dispositional and situational forms as an interpretive framework and working hypothesis rather than as a finding derived from the reviewed evidence, since no included study operationalises these distinctions in this age group. Across a small, geographically concentrated body of evidence that rests on a limited number of independent samples, higher self-forgiveness is associated with lower depression, rumination, and suicidal ideation and with greater life satisfaction and self-esteem, frequently operating as a resilience factor that buffers the impact of adversity and negative self-evaluation; a single longitudinal study found an association with mortality only among participants with more years of schooling. We discuss the scarcity of validated, age-appropriate measures, the difficulty of separating self-forgiveness from adjacent constructs such as self-compassion, and how forgiveness-based, compassion-focused, and life-review interventions could be integrated into mental-health promotion for older adults.

items.title: Characterising reach and uptake of a national digital mental health service in the Australian community: This Way Up.
items.authors: Shiner CT, Li I, Olsen N, Roberge P, Vasiliadis HM, Millard M, Mahoney AE.
items.journal: International journal of mental health systems

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Digital mental health services (DMHS) can increase the accessibility and scalability of evidence-based mental health care. DMHS have been integrated within health systems and shown to be clinically effective for anxiety and depressive disorders, but the nature of service reach within routine community care remains under-explored. This study aimed to characterise reach and uptake of an Australian digital mental health service (THIS WAY UP), describe the socio-demography of routine service users and investigate predictors of treatment uptake in a large community sample.

sections.heading: Methods

items.title: Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms, Motivational Quality and Academic Performance Among Türkiye-Born and Early-Arriving Syrian-Background Students: The Moderating Role of Academic Language Proficiency.
items.authors: Çınaroğlu M, Yılmazer E.

sections.text: Many Syrian students in Turkish schools were born in Türkiye or arrived before school entry, yet their post-traumatic stress and its links with schooling are poorly documented. In this observational two-contact study, we examined whether post-traumatic stress symptoms were associated with academic performance among 407 Türkiye-born or early-arriving (at or before age five) Syrian-background students in grades 5-12 (mean age 13.84 years), recruited non-randomly across eight provinces; whether indirect associations through autonomous motivation and amotivation were evident; and whether academic Turkish proficiency conditioned the motivation-performance path. Symptoms and motivation were measured at first contact; first-term grade averages were obtained approximately ten weeks later. Within this recruited sample, 38.6% scored at or above the CRIES-13 screening cut-off. Symptom severity was inversely associated with performance (β = -0.26), net of depressive and anxiety symptoms and recorded absence. Under an assumed ordering in which symptoms precede motivation, the indirect coefficients through autonomous motivation and amotivation represented 42.7% of the modelled total association, with a direct association remaining. In an exploratory analysis, the indirect association through autonomous motivation was weaker among students with the lowest academic Turkish proficiency (index of moderated mediation = -0.029, 95% CI -0.054 to -0.008). Because symptoms and motivation were measured concurrently, general cognitive ability was not assessed, and sampling was non-probability, these associations are hypothesis-generating and call for longitudinal and intervention research.

items.title: Amplitude-Frequency Characteristic as a Novel Eye-Tracking Diagnostic Feature: A Pilot Study on an Open ADHD Dataset.
items.authors: Nikulchev E, Kosenkov AN, Sokolov A, Alexeenko A, Ilin D.

sections.text: The frequency characteristic of biological systems is a sensitive tool for describing physiological dynamics, yet it has been virtually unused in pupillometry. A novel eye-tracking feature is proposed-the amplitude-frequency characteristic (AFC) of the "stimulus-pupil size" system-and evaluated as a candidate diagnostic marker on an open ADHD dataset. After quality control, 61 sessions (18 controls, 27 unmedicated ADHD, 16 on-medication ADHD) were analyzed. The AFC of the raw diameter signal reveals a systematic elevation of AFC amplitude in ADHD across the 0.5-30 Hz range, strongest in the 20-30 Hz band (Cohen's d = +0.995, p = 0.0034). This is a pilot and methodology- and reproducibility-focused study. At the individual diagnostic level, a normative composite z-score of three bands (10-15, 15-20, 20-30 Hz), computed relative to the control group with fixed weights and no training, reaches an ROC-AUC = 0.788 (Ctrl vs. off-ADHD: p = 0.0012). At the group level, a linear discriminant projection of the eight-band profile reaches an ROC-AUC = 0.854. The inter-individual variability of within-subject AFC stability is reduced by a factor of 2.97 in unmedicated ADHD ( p = 0.0085) and normalizes under methylphenidate (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0067, n = 17). The widely used ratio of high- to low-frequency AFC amplitude yields an inflated ROC-AUC of 0.865 on the pre-filtered signal, but only 0.63 on the raw signal. All diagnostic claims are exploratory. The proposed normative feature is simple, interpretable, requires no training set, and can be computed from a single pupil recording.
