items.title: Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria and Documented Schizophrenia: A Population-Based Matched Case-Control Study and Its Implications for Personalized Somatic Care in Severe Mental Illness.
items.authors: Magen E, Magen I, Geishin A, Merzon E, Green I, Golan-Cohen A, Vinker S, Israel A.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a treatable mast cell-mediated disease whose documentation requires repeated outpatient contact. We tested whether documented schizophrenia differs between individuals with probable CSU and matched controls. Methods: We conducted a population-based 1:5 matched case-control study of Leumit Health Services (Israel) electronic health records, 2003-2024. We matched 9235 members with algorithm-defined probable CSU (≥2 urticaria encounters ≥42 days apart plus antihistamine dispensing) to 46,175 controls on date of birth, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, enrolment year, and primary-care branch. Psychiatrist-assigned schizophrenia up to 20 years before and 10 years after the index date was analyzed by conditional logistic regression, with sensitivity and quantitative bias analyses. Results: Schizophrenia was documented in 0.32% of cases and 0.70% of controls (matched OR 0.47; 95% CI, 0.32-0.68); 70% of affected cases were diagnosed before CSU. Results were consistent across estimation methods, sex and age strata, and registry-based ascertainment (OR 0.36; 95% CI, 0.22-0.61), whereas depression and anxiety were more frequent in cases. Antipsychotic dispensing was lower for long-acting injectable and high-potency agents, although no individual comparison remained significant after adjustment for multiplicity. Conclusions: Schizophrenia was documented about half as often in individuals with probable CSU as in matched controls. The data show an inverse association between two documented conditions and do not establish its cause. Limitations: The CSU algorithm has not been validated against chart review in this database, and control eligibility used post-index information, examined by bias analysis only. Whether CSU is under-recognized in schizophrenia remains a hypothesis requiring dedicated study.

items.title: Undergraduate Nursing Students' Perceived Appropriateness of Coercive Measures in Psychiatric Care and Associated Factors: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Anastasi G, Latina R, Bambi S.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Coercive measures raise ethical and clinical concerns in psychiatric care. Although nurses' attitudes have been widely investigated, little is known about how nursing students evaluate coercive practices before entering professional practice. This study examined nursing students' perceived appropriateness of physical restraint, pharmacological restraint, and locked-door policies, and explored associated sociodemographic, educational, and psychosocial factors. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among nursing students in Italy. Three items assessed perceived appropriateness, and validated scales measured depression, anxiety, stress, stigma toward mental illness, and humanization of care. Analyses included descriptive, bivariate, multivariable linear regression, and ordinal logistic sensitivity analyses. Results: Among 378 students, appropriateness differed across interventions ( p < 0.001), with the highest ratings for locked-door policies and the lowest for physical restraint. In adjusted linear models, third-year enrolment was associated with lower ratings for physical restraint (β = -0.227), pharmacological restraint (β = -0.292), and locked-door policies (β = -0.207), consistent with ordinal analyses. Higher physical-restraint ratings were associated with younger age (β = -0.125), male gender (β = 0.107), Central Italy (β = 0.121), and academic satisfaction (β = 0.223). Second-year enrolment was associated with lower pharmacological-restraint ratings (β = -0.144). Higher locked-door ratings were associated with non-belief (β = 0.109), previous mental health education (β = 0.224), and stress (β = 0.232), whereas anxiety was inversely associated (β = -0.212). Stigma showed no significant adjusted associations; humanization findings differed between models. Explanatory power was modest (adjusted R^2 = 0.052-0.092). Conclusions: Students evaluated coercive measures differently, with shared and intervention-specific correlates. Nursing education should critically address environmental restrictions, patient autonomy, and least-restrictive care. Longitudinal research is needed to clarify the contribution of educational and clinical experiences.

items.title: Identifying clinical markers of imminent risk: the challenge of deciding which patients are about to have a crisis.
items.authors: Lew RA, Androsenko M, Liang MH, Ferguson R, Ostacher M.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Clinicians need markers of imminent medical crises. We constructed odds ratios (OR's) from short-term risk markers based on consecutive monthly questionnaire responses to predict an imminent crisis. These markers should improve clinical decisions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: For response scores of k=0 to K we chose a threshold T (1≤T≤K), defined 'low risk' as a score <T, 'high risk' as a score >=T, and OR=Odds (high risk of a crisis)/Odds(low risk of a crisis). Patient responses in months 0-3 and other intervals were summarized in five ways, as the mean, maximum, minimum, first, and last response.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: From a clinical trial comparing lithium to placebo to see if lithium reduced the risk of suicidal behavior, notable month 0-3 short-term risk OR's included: Columbia Suicide Severity Risk Scale: maximum C-SSRS score ≥4 (suicidal ideation) had OR=5.57 (3.08-10.16). Patient Health Questionnaire: Last PHQ-9 total score ≥16 (depression) had OR=2.45 (1.41-4.26). Internal State Scale: ISS Last Well-being score ≤3 had OR=3.42 (1.50-7.82)].

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Odds ratios varied by starting month and interval width. They complement long-term risk estimates and promise to improve risk prediction for many diseases.

items.title: Comparative TWAS suggests predominantly shared ageing-related gene expression patterns with quantitative differences in treatment-resistant schizophrenia.
items.authors: Cheung N.

sections.text: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) affects roughly 20-30% of people diagnosed with schizophrenia and is linked to poorer clinical and functional outcomes. Its molecular basis, however, remains only partly understood. In this study, we integrated transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) results from two large schizophrenia genome-wide association studies (GWAS): one reflecting broad schizophrenia liability and another using a clozapine-treated phenotype as a proxy for treatment resistance. These TWAS profiles were intersected with 48 curated ageing-related gene sets covering NAD metabolism, mitochondrial function, cellular senescence, synaptic plasticity, complement signalling and glial biology. In the original curated analysis, both general schizophrenia and TRS showed enrichment in long-term potentiation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, NAD and sirtuin pathways, complement-mediated pruning and glial signatures. This pattern is consistent with shared ageing-related vulnerability across schizophrenia phenotypes. At the same time, TRS showed selected quantitative and directional differences at key nodes within this shared architecture. Key differences included nominal shifts in PPP1R1B (DARPP-32), stronger influence of PPP3CC, DRD2, DRD3, DRD5 and synaptic vesicle genes, broader mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation burden, a stronger negative NAMPT signal with TFAM elevation, mixed mitochondrial sirtuin signals, elevated SLC2A1 and amplified complement enrichment. Sensitivity analyses showed that while most pathway enrichments were attenuated under stricter TWAS-filtered membership, formal matched-tissue key-gene tests confirmed significant differences for only four key genes: TFAM, SIRT5, SLC2A1 and C4A, and high concordance persisted in a broader Hallmark comparator set. The findings support a working model in which TRS shares broad ageing-related transcriptomic architecture with schizophrenia but shows selected quantitative and directional differences at key nodes, potentially constraining circuit adaptability under chronic D2 receptor blockade. The identified gene modules provide a hypothesis-generating foundation for future biomarker studies and stratified adjunctive trials targeting mitochondrial resilience, NAD metabolism and metabolic flexibility; however, extensive independent replication, functional validation and clinical testing would be required before any translational application.

items.title: Estimating first episode psychosis (FEP) incidence rates using U.S. claims data: a need for standardization.
items.authors: Seiber EE, Sridhar S, Hasenstab KA, Chi E, Breitborde NJK.

sections.text: This brief's objective was to examine variation in first-episode psychosis (FEP) incidence rates by applying previously published study criteria to U.S. MarketScan claims data. Estimated FEP incidence rates ranged from 20 to 163 per 100,000 individuals, highlighting the need for standardization. Factors contributing to this variation included ICD coding definitions, age range, duration of continuous enrollment prior to the index diagnosis, minimum number of psychosis-related claims, and antipsychotic prescription requirements.

items.title: Identification of robust speech-based markers of negative symptom severity in schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
items.authors: Spilka MJ, Robin J, Nikzad AH, Behbehani L, Berretta S, Xu M, Kane JM, Simpson W, Tang SX.

sections.text: There is growing interest in using digital health technologies to overcome limitations of traditional negative symptom assessment in schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD). For example, computerized speech analysis has been used to quantify speech and language changes associated with negative symptom severity in SSD. However, the large number of speech features and variability across studies make it difficult to determine the features with the greatest clinical utility. The present study aimed to identify the most robust speech-based markers of negative symptom severity by comprehensively evaluating their psychometric properties in a sample of individuals with SSD. Data were analyzed from 62 SSD participants who completed clinical assessments and speech tasks at baseline and follow-up visits. Thirty-eight acoustic and linguistic speech features were evaluated for test-retest reliability within visits, associations with clinician-rated negative symptoms, convergent and discriminant validity, specificity for negative symptom severity, and associations with participant clinical and demographic characteristics. Consistency of findings was evaluated across the two study visits, treating the second visit as a within-study replication sample. Three features (speech proportion, speech rate, unfilled pauses) consistently showed adequate or better reliability, correlations with negative symptoms across tasks and visits, and further demonstrated discriminant validity, specificity, and lack of associations with antipsychotic medication and extrapyramidal symptoms. Speech rate also consistently demonstrated convergent validity with an alternative negative symptom measure and was the most reliable feature when evaluated at the level of a single task administration. These findings advance the clinical validation of speech-based digital biomarkers for negative symptom assessment in SSD.

items.title: Brexpiprazole augmentation of aripiprazole once-monthly in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: A 12-week, open-label, randomised controlled pilot trial (BREATH-JS study).
items.authors: Takekita Y, Takano C, Koshikawa Y, Funatsuki T, Takahashi A, Murase Y, Bando H, Minami S, Shimamoto Y, Shimizu T, Kojima Y, Tanaka Y, Sunada N, Ogata H, Aoki N, Kato M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Aripiprazole once-monthly (AOM) cannot be escalated beyond 400 mg because of its formulation, and evidence on how to manage residual symptoms in patients maintained on AOM is scarce.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To examine the efficacy and tolerability of brexpiprazole augmentation in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders receiving AOM maintenance treatment.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: A 12-week, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised controlled pilot trial.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Thirty outpatients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder who had been receiving AOM for at least 2 months (all on 400 mg every 4 weeks) and had a Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score of 120 or less were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to brexpiprazole augmentation or AOM continuation, with concealed allocation; 29 (brexpiprazole augmentation, 14; AOM continuation, 15) were analysed. The primary outcome was the change in the PANSS total score to week 12, analysed with a mixed-effects model for repeated measures.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The adjusted between-group difference in the PANSS total score at week 12 was -12.4 (95% CI, -21.2 to -3.5; P = 0.008), favouring brexpiprazole augmentation, and this difference was apparent from week 4. abstract.text:
Aripiprazole once-monthly (AOM) cannot be escalated beyond 400 mg because of its formulation, and evidence on how to manage residual symptoms in patients maintained on AOM is scarce.

To examine the efficacy and tolerability of brexpiprazole augmentation in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders receiving AOM maintenance treatment.

A 12-week, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised controlled pilot trial.

Thirty outpatients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder who had been receiving AOM for at least 2 months (all on 400 mg every 4 weeks) and had a Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score of 120 or less were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to brexpiprazole augmentation or AOM continuation, with concealed allocation; 29 (brexpiprazole augmentation, 14; AOM continuation, 15) were analysed. The primary outcome was the change in the PANSS total score to week 12, analysed with a mixed-effects model for repeated measures.

The adjusted between-group difference in the PANSS total score at week 12 was -12.4 (95% CI, -21.2 to -3.5; P = 0.008), favouring brexpiprazole augmentation, and this difference was apparent from week 4. Greater improvement was seen across all Marder five factors. A reduction of 20% or more occurred only in the brexpiprazole augmentation group (6/14, 42.9%; AOM continuation, 0/15; P = 0.006). Adverse events did not differ between groups; no worsening in body weight, metabolic parameters, or prolactin was observed, and akathisia decreased in the brexpiprazole augmentation group ( P = 0.011).

Brexpiprazole augmentation of AOM maintenance treatment improved the PANSS total score and was well tolerated. As this was an open-label, exploratory pilot trial, the findings are hypothesis-generating and require verification in larger, blinded, randomised controlled trials.

items.title: Association Between 1-Hydroxypyrene and Common Mental Health Problems Among Urban Traffic Wardens in Kolkata City, India.
items.authors: Sen S, Saha I, Saha A, Basu A, Pattnaik M, Bhowmik K, Das A, Dhar S, Mukherjee S, Das P, Pati S.

sections.text: Air pollution exposure significantly affects the central nervous system and contributes to various mental health issues. Traffic wardens are subjected to increased workplace exposure to numerous air contaminants, notably polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), resulting in a heightened risk of mental health issues. This study was carried out to estimate urine levels of 1-hydroxypyrene (1-OHP) as a biomarker of PAH exposure and to assess its association with mental health among traffic wardens working in the traffic department. A total of 250 wardens participated in the study, with 237 being males and 13 being females; 3.80% of traffic workers reported depression, 12.20% had anxiety symptoms, and 11.00% had stress among the male group. The mean 1-OHP level was 0.25 ± 0.16 µmol/mol creatinine among the male population. Comparing three psychological-distress measures with 1-OHP levels showed a statistically significant ( p < 0.05) correlation with depression and stress. Additionally, urinary 1-OHP was positively associated with depression ( β = 4.26, 95% CI: 2.81-5.71, p < 0.01), anxiety ( β = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.29-4.55, p < 0.01) and stress ( β = 5.20, 95% CI: 2.59-7.81, p < 0.01) after adjustment for age, education, diet, tobacco use and alcohol consumption. In addition to the regression models, increases of 17.30% in depression, 13.90% in anxiety, and 12.70% in stress scores were significant at p < 0.05. Exposure to PAHs through increased 1-OHP was found to be associated with mental health conditions like depression and stress.

items.title: Neonicotinoids and Mental Health: Mechanistic, Preclinical and Epidemiological Evidence for a Transdiagnostic Neurodevelopmental Risk.
items.authors: Rosas-Sánchez GU, Soria-Fregozo C, Ortíz-Sánchez EH, Avalos-García S, Rodríguez-Landa JF, Germán-Ponciano LJ, Ramos de Robles SL, Flores-Soto ME, Fernández-Demeneghi R, Pérez-Vega MI, Soriano-Hernández AD.

sections.text: Neonicotinoid insecticides (imidacloprid, clothianidin, thiacloprid, acetamiprid, thiamethoxam, nitenpyram, dinotefuran) were developed as insect-selective nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) agonists and have long been regarded as safe for vertebrates. However, parent compounds and, more potently, desnitro metabolites such as DN-imidacloprid act on mammalian α4β2 and α7 nAChRs with nicotine-like potency, implicating cholinergic circuits central to cognition, mood, and reward. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and epidemiological evidence linking neonicotinoid exposure to neuropsychiatric risk. Mechanistically, these compounds promote glial activation, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and gut microbiota alterations that converge on hippocampal and limbic dysfunction. Rodent and invertebrate studies show sex-, dose-, and exposure-window-dependent effects on anxiety-, depression-, and cognition-like behaviors, with developmental exposure mirroring prenatal nicotine effects. Human data, although limited, are convergent: poisoning case series document acute neuropsychiatric symptoms; biomonitoring studies in China, Japan, and Sri Lanka associate urinary metabolites with depression, anxiety, and a recognizable "neo-nicotinic" symptom cluster; in Mexico, studies of agricultural populations link pesticide mixtures to psychological distress, although neonicotinoid biomarkers have not yet been measured in that setting; and pediatric cohorts in China and Ecuador link prenatal and childhood exposure to impaired neurodevelopment, emotional symptoms, and hyperactivity. Collectively, this evidence is consistent with neonicotinoids being an underrecognized environmental risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, although the human data remain too fragmented to support causal inference and underscores the need for dedicated cohorts, expanded biomonitoring, and mechanistic research to inform regulatory assessment.

items.title: Multi-omics integration identifies COQ8A in excitatory neurons as a protective gene in major depressive disorder.
items.authors: Dong CL, Liu XY, Wang XC, Kuang L, Wang W, Jiang ZH, Ran LY.

sections.text: The pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD) remains insufficiently understood, which may be due to the limitations of bulk tissue analyses in addressing cellular heterogeneity. In this study, we applied a comprehensive approach combining brain cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait loci data, MDD genome-wide association study summary statistics, and MDD single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data, with the aim of identifying cell-specific key genes. The utilization of summary-based mendelian randomization and two-sample mendelian randomization analyses resulted in the discovery of 26 candidate genes, of which 15 exhibited strong colocalization signals across four distinct brain cell types. Combining snRNA-seq data analysis, we discovered that COQ8A is down-regulated in excitatory neurons (Ex) and LATS1 is up-regulated in oligodendrocytes in MDD patients. These findings were further validated by mice chronic social defeat stress models, which demonstrated significant downregulation of COQ8A in Ex of prefrontal cortex (PFC). Functional analysis suggests a relationship between the down-regulated expression of COQ8A in Ex from the MDD group and impaired energy metabolism, mitochondrial function, and protein synthesis. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated that eight antidepressants bind to COQ8A with high affinity, with Escitalopram and Paroxetine effectively stabilizing its active sites. Our findings indicate that COQ8A in Ex of the PFC, associated with mitochondrial function, may serve as a key protective gene in MDD. Furthermore, COQ8A emerges as a promising therapeutic target for precision antidepressant treatment. This study enhances our understanding of the neurobiological basis of MDD at the single-cell level.

items.title: Mental Health of University Students in València Following the 2024 Cutoff Low (DANA): A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Casino-García AM, Molero D, Alonso-Larza L, Llinares-Insa LI.
items.journal: European journal of investigation in health, psychology and education
items.journal_abbrev: Eur J Investig Health Psychol Educ

sections.text: Natural disasters are stress factors that can affect university students' mental health. During the floods caused by the 2024 cutoff low (DANA in Spanish) in Valencia, the media recognized the remarkable volunteer work carried out by students during the recovery effort. This study assessed the consequences of the DANA event on stress, well-being, and distress symptomatology (depression and anxiety) among 793 Spanish university students, 593 of whom were enrolled in affected universities. The results revealed that, compared with those who were not exposed, students who were exposed to DANA had higher levels of positive affect and life satisfaction alongside fewer depressive symptoms. However, participants who experienced direct losses evidenced lower levels of well-being and greater distress, as did women and individuals combining studies with work. Structural equation modeling enabled the testing of a theoretically specified structural model between perceived stress and mental health. In both groups, stress affected anxiety and depression directly. Nevertheless, among those affected by DANA, stress was associated with life satisfaction solely indirectly via affect. These findings underscore the coexistence of adaptation and vulnerability processes in the aftermath of the disaster and highlight the need to focus the actions of higher education institutions on prevention and psychosocial support.

items.title: Psychometric Properties of the Spanish Version of the University Student Stressors Questionnaire (USSQ): Structure, Reliability, Validity, and Measurement Invariance.
items.authors: Beranuy M, Yllanes-Lizarraga S, Esteban-Rezusta E, Kamtsios S, Karagiannopoulou E, Beyebach M, Rivera D.
items.journal: European journal of investigation in health, psychology and education
items.journal_abbrev: Eur J Investig Health Psychol Educ

sections.text: The scarcity of psychometrically robust instruments limits the assessment of academic stressors among Spanish university students. This study aimed to adapt the University Student Stressors Questionnaire (USSQ) to the Spanish context and evaluate its psychometric properties in a sample of undergraduate and postgraduate students. An instrumental, cross-sectional census survey design was used to evaluate the psychometric properties of the instrument. A total of 4925 students from a Spanish public university participated. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance analyses (by sex, gender, and study level), and convergent validity analyses with measures of depression, anxiety, and stress (DASS-21) and psychological well-being (Ryff's PWB) were conducted. The final 27-item, seven-factor model demonstrated optimal fit and adequate reliability (McDonald's omega: 0.73-0.89). Partial measurement invariance was achieved for sex and gender, and full invariance for study level. Convergent validity was supported through positive correlations with psychological distress and negative correlations with well-being. The University Student Stressors Questionnaire (USSQ) is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing academic stressors in the Spanish university population. "Fear of failure" emerges as the most prominent factor associated with psychological distress.

items.title: Human factors shaping engagement with a digital treatment platform among individuals with lived experience of addiction.
items.authors: Bormann NL, Smith JL, Paul MM, Lai B, Stoppel C, Tuen KA, Cox DM, Breitinger SA, Williams MD, Oesterle TS.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, yet access to care remains limited. Digital interventions have been investigated as a means to expand treatment access, but individuals routinely disengage from them. We evaluated the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability of a digital platform being tested as part of a collaborative care management-based intervention for SUD treatment in under-resourced areas to identify human factors influencing feasibility, usability, and accessibility.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants were adults with lived experience of addiction and related treatment. They engaged with the digital treatment platform for one week, then completed semi-structured interviews exploring their experience, followed by the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, Feasibility of Intervention Measure, and System Usability Scale. Template-based rapid analysis identified themes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 18 individuals ( n  = 12 females) completed all assessments. Heavy text, lack of customization, and inconsistent notifications hindered usability. Participants felt assigned goals should match an individual's circumstances and resources available to them to support utilization. Participants desired personalization, integration with existing recovery supports, and features that encouraged routine use. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility had respective means of 3.4 (95%CI = 3.0-3.9), 3.3 (95%CI = 2.8-3.9), and 3.4 (95%CI = 2.8-4.0) on 5-point scales with a neutral midpoint of 3. Usability scores approached the commonly used benchmark of 68 (mean=67.6, SD = 15.0).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Digital interventions suffer from heavy disengagement. These findings suggest that digital interventions should fit the end-user's needs and surrounding environment and be both person- and context-specific. Attention to these human factors may improve usability and accessibility, while also limiting additional barriers in under-resourced areas.

items.title: Antibiotic-Associated Encephalopathy in Geriatric Patients: A Neglected Challenge.
items.authors: Djukic M, Seele J, Bodilsen J, Nau R.

sections.text: Background: The aging brain is more vulnerable to many medical drugs, including antibiotics. In geriatrics, the differentiation between symptoms of the infection and adverse effects of the antibiotic therapy can be difficult. Whereas most other drugs are prescribed as lifelong or very long treatments, antibiotics are the drug class most frequently initiated by the largest number of different medical specialties. Since the geriatric rule "start low, go slow" does not apply for antibiotics, the risk of immediate side effects as a consequence of exposure of a geriatric patient to the full drug dose is relatively high. Method: For this narrative review we searched PUBMED using defined search terms. Results: Age, impaired renal function, and a reduced cognitive reserve are the strongest individual predictors of central nervous toxicity of antibiotics. Antibiotic-associated encephalopathy can be divided into three different forms, which partly overlap: (1) hallucinations and delusions starting within hours to days after the first dose (predominantly associated with fluoroquinolones and macrolides, rarely with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim or other antibiotics); (2) myoclonus and epileptic seizures starting within hours to days after the first dose (mainly caused by cephalosporines, penicillins, and carbapenems); (3) vertigo, nystagmus and ataxia caused by metronidazole and optical neuropathy, vertigo, mental obtundation and epileptic seizures as a consequence of the functional antagonism of isoniazid and vitamin B6. Conclusions: The contribution of antibiotics to the development of delirium, myoclonus and epileptic seizures is likely underestimated. Renal failure and neurological or psychiatric abnormalities prior to infection are the main predisposing factors for antibiotic-associated encephalopathy in old age.

items.title: Acute Effects of Resistance Exercise Volume on Physiological and Psychological Outcomes in Adults Diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder: A Randomized Crossover Study.
items.authors: Campos JMS, Quizzini GH, Dos Santos MAA, Amorim TAM, Cruz AFOD, Jokura MS, Trombetta-Lima M, Nascimento C, Jímenez-Maldonado A, Schuch FB, Neves LM, Rossi FE.
items.journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology

sections.text: Background and Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate the acute effects of resistance exercise volume on physiological and psychological outcomes in adults with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). Methods: This randomized crossover trial included adults aged 18-59 years with MDD. Participants completed two resistance exercise conditions: high-volume resistance exercise (HV-RE; four sets of 10-12 RM) and low-volume resistance exercise (LV-RE; two sets of 10-12 RM). Both protocols consisted of 10 full-body exercises, with 60 s rest between sets and 90 s between exercises. Total training volume was calculated as sets x repetitions x load (kg). Blood lactate concentration was assessed at rest and 3 min post-exercise. Affective responses were measured using the Feeling Scale (FS), training self-efficacy using the Perceived Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale (PESE), and mood states using the Brunel Mood Scale (BRUMS). Results: Twenty-four participants [20 women (83.3%)] were included. Training volume (3944.8 ± 1471.5 vs. 7603.9 ± 2800.2 kg, p < 0.001, d = 1.64) and RPE (6.2 ± 1.3 vs. 8.2 ± 1.3, p < 0.001, d = 1.54) were lower in LV-RE than in HV-RE. Both conditions increased blood lactate concentration ( p < 0.001, η^2 = 0.77), with no between-condition differences ( p = 0.184). Significant main effects of time were observed for total mood state ( p < 0.001, η2 = 0.54), depression ( p = 0.025, η2 = 0.20), anger ( p < 0.001, η2 = 0.47), vigor ( p < 0.001, η2 = 0.53), and fatigue ( p = 0.037, η2 = 0.18), whereas tension and confusion did not change significantly ( p > 0.05). A significant improvement in affective responses was also observed ( p < 0.001, η2 = 0.44), with no significant condition × time interactions ( p > 0.05). There were no significant changes in self-efficacy. Conclusions: Both resistance exercise protocols were associated with acute changes in mood states and improved affective responses, alongside increased blood lactate concentrations, with no statistically significant differences in these changes detected between conditions. LV-RE elicited lower perceived exertion than HV-RE, suggesting that lower-volume resistance exercise may be a less demanding option for adults with MDD.

There were no significant changes in self-efficacy. Conclusions: Both resistance exercise protocols were associated with acute changes in mood states and improved affective responses, alongside increased blood lactate concentrations, with no statistically significant differences in these changes detected between conditions. LV-RE elicited lower perceived exertion than HV-RE, suggesting that lower-volume resistance exercise may be a less demanding option for adults with MDD.

items.title: Association Between Anti-Ro52 Antibody Concentration and Documented Depression in Patients with Sjögren's Disease: A Retrospective Observational Study.
items.authors: Lerotić II, Martinović Kaliterna D, Krstulović DM.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Depression is a clinically relevant neuropsychiatric manifestation of Sjögren's disease, although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Autoimmune and neuroinflammatory processes, including the potential role of autoantibodies, may contribute to its development. This study aimed to investigate the association between anti-Ro antibodies, with particular emphasis on anti-Ro52, and the presence of depression in patients with Sjögren's disease and to explore whether quantitative anti-Ro52 antibody levels may provide patient-level information relevant to a more personalized assessment of neuropsychiatric manifestations. Methods: This retrospective, observational, cross-sectional study included 141 adult patients with Sjögren's disease treated at the University Hospital of Split between 2020 and 2023. Depression was defined as a documented diagnosis supported by psychiatric evaluation. The association between anti-Ro52 antibody concentration and depression was assessed using Firth's penalized logistic regression, adjusted for age and sex, with correction for multiple testing using the false discovery rate procedure. A sensitivity analysis was performed after restricting the analysis to patients with primary Sjögren's disease. Results: Depression was documented in 16/141 patients (11.3%). Anti-Ro52 concentrations were available for 111 patients, including 13 with depression. Higher anti-Ro52 concentrations were significantly associated with lower odds of depression. A one-standard-deviation increase in anti-Ro52 concentration was associated with 70% lower odds of depression (OR 0.30; 95% CI 0.12-0.61; p < 0.001). The association remained significant after multiple-testing correction (overall FDR-adjusted p = 0.046). The inverse association remained significant in the sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with primary Sjögren's disease (OR per 1-SD increase = 0.38; 95% CI 0.14-0.82; p = 0.013). Conclusions: Higher anti-Ro52 antibody concentrations were associated with lower odds of documented depression in patients with Sjögren's disease after adjustment for age and sex. These findings suggest that quantitative serological profiling may provide patient-level information relevant to a more personalized assessment of neuropsychiatric manifestations. However, prospective studies using standardized depression assessments are required to determine the clinical relevance and potential utility of anti-Ro52 levels in individualized patients.

items.title: Effect of long-acting injectable antipsychotics on antipsychotic dose changes in patients with schizophrenia.
items.authors: Suzuki T, Okinaga K, Abe T, Kawai M, Ochiai M, Enomoto R, Yanagawa T, Aida K, Hayasaka S.
items.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical health care and sciences

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics are commonly used to address poor adherence. However, their effects on prescribed oral doses remain unclear. This study investigated LAI-related changes in antipsychotic dose.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective study included 33 Japanese patients with schizophrenia who began treatment with one of the following LAIs: risperidone long-acting injection biweekly (RLAI), paliperidone palmitate long-acting injection monthly (PP), or aripiprazole hydrate prolonged release injection monthly (AOM). Prescribed drugs and doses were recorded at seven time points, from 4 weeks before to 24 weeks after LAI initiation. Doses were converted to chlorpromazine (CP) equivalents, and dose changes were assessed. Effects of disorder duration and age at LAI initiation were also evaluated.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After LAI initiation, significant dose increases were observed in PP- and AOM-treated patients but not in those receiving RLAI. In AOM-treated patients, %CP changes varied by initial dose, with dose maintenance at < 400 mg and decreases at 400-800 mg and ≥ 800 mg. A significant effect of initial dose, number of concomitant antipsychotics, and disorder duration before LAI initiation was also found (p < 0.05).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings underscore the importance of follow-up and dose reassessment after starting LAI treatment.

items.title: Association Between Perceived Negative Workplace Gossip, Mental Health and Professional Life Among Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study in Greece.
items.authors: Galanis P, Moisoglou I, Triantafillaki A, Velonaki VS, Pesiridis T, Katsiroumpa A.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Negative workplace gossip has been linked to nurses' mental health and professional life. The aim of this study was to examine the association between perceived negative workplace gossip, mental health and professional life among nurses. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Greece during May 2026. We used validated scales to measure the study variables: Perceived Negative Workplace Gossip Scale, Patient Health Questionnaire-4, Quiet Quitting Scale, Utrecht Work Engagement Scale-3, Organization-Based Self-Esteem Scale, Single-Item Job Satisfaction measure, and Single-Item Burnout measure. Also, we used a single-item measure to examine nurses' turnover intention. Results: We found a significant positive association between perceived negative workplace gossip and both anxiety ( p = 0.012), and depression symptoms ( p < 0.001). Moreover, multivariable linear regression analysis identified a positive association between perceived negative workplace gossip and three dimensions of quiet quitting; (1) detachment ( p = 0.001), (2) lack of initiative ( p < 0.001), and (3) lack of motivation ( p < 0.001). Also, we found a positive association between perceived negative workplace gossip and job burnout ( p = 0.009). Multivariable linear regression analysis showed a negative association between perceived negative workplace gossip and work engagement ( p < 0.001), organization-based self-esteem ( p < 0.001), and job satisfaction ( p < 0.001). Additionally, multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that higher level of perceived negative workplace gossip was associated with higher odds of turnover intention ( p = 0.001). Conclusions: Perceived negative workplace gossip showed statistically significant but small associations with anxiety, depression, quiet quitting, work engagement, organization-based self-esteem, job satisfaction, job burnout, and turnover intention. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations do not establish causality. Our results support attention to the relational climate of nursing units, while longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine whether reducing negative workplace gossip improves nurses' mental health and professional outcomes.

items.title: Lead (Pb)-Induced Neuroinflammation in the Developing and Aging Brain.
items.authors: Mendes HW, Freeman JL.

sections.text: Dysregulation of neuroinflammation has been implicated as a key mechanism in the etiology of several conditions of both a developmental and degenerative nature. Neuroinflammation is also one of the main mechanisms by which contamination with certain environmental pollutants-like lead (Pb)-disrupts the central nervous system (CNS), leading to significant neurological damage. A growing body of evidence indicates a potential link between lead exposure to the onset of neurodevelopmental disorders-such as Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)-and neurodegenerative conditions, like those observed in Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Important pathways have been identified in the context of lead exposure and association with neurological conditions; however, the precise mechanisms by which lead-induced neuroinflammation might be associated with these conditions are largely unknown. Inflammation of the CNS can be considered a key element in the convergence of lead-induced neuroinflammation and neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative conditions. This review contextualizes aspects of neuroinflammatory responses upon lead exposure and discusses how these disruptions overlap with the onset of neurodevelopmental disorders, such as ASD and ADHD, and neurodegenerative diseases, such as PD and AD. We focus on recent developments in the field of neuroinflammation within these different contexts and discuss different hypotheses, sex as a biological variable, and areas in need of further investigation.

items.title: Prenatal Exposure to Polychlorinated Biphenyls in Indoor Air and Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
items.authors: Fleischer NL, Curtis AB, Wils RS, Meyer HW, Hougaard KS, Bonde JPE, Tøttenborg SS, Deen L.

sections.text: Lower-chlorinated polychlorinated biphenyls (LC-PCBs) likely act through toxicological mechanisms distinct from higher-chlorinated PCBs, which have been studied more extensively. Although LC-PCBs more readily cross the placenta and may disrupt foetal development, their contributions to neurodevelopmental disorders remain unclear. We aimed to investigate the association between prenatal exposure to LC-PCBs in indoor air and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We included 3797 children whose mothers lived in one of two partially PCB-contaminated housing areas in Greater Copenhagen at some point during the 3.6-year period before conception through pregnancy. PCB exposure was based on indoor air measurements of seven indicator PCBs (PCB-28, -52, -101, -118, -138, -153, and -180) and cumulated according to years of maternal residence. ADHD and ASD diagnoses were obtained from national registers. We estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using Cox regression models. Prenatal PCB exposure ≥ 300 ng/m^3 × year was associated with higher risk of ADHD (aHR 1.53 95% CI: 1.09-2.15) and showed a tendency towards higher risk of ASD (aHR 1.35 95% CI: 0.87-2.08) compared with exposure < 300 ng/m^3 × year. Our findings suggest that prenatal exposure to LC-PCBs in indoor air may disrupt neurodevelopmental programming and increase risk of ADHD and ASD when living one year with levels above the Danish Health Authority's lower action level (300 ng/m^3).

items.title: Chinese international students' mental health in Western universities: a scoping review.
items.authors: Zhao J, Shi K, Barnett P, Pilling S, Fonagy P.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Over one million Chinese international students (CIS) are currently enrolled in higher education abroad, predominantly in Western universities. The volume of research on CIS mental health has increased steadily in recent years, with evidence indicating poorer outcomes compared to both domestic and other international student groups. However, comprehensive syntheses and understanding of this literature remain limited. We conducted a scoping review to map the evidence on CIS mental health in Western higher education settings, to examine the strength and gaps of the evidence base, and to inform future research and support provision.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Based on a pre-registered strategy, we systematically searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, ERIC, and CINAHL from inception to 10 December 2025. Grey literature was also searched (including PsycEXTRA, BASE, medRxiv, and PsyArXiv). Articles were reviewed for inclusion/exclusion by 2 authors.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: This scoping review integrates findings from 225 reports, examining three core areas: the prevalence of mental health issues, existing interventions, and factors influencing mental health and psychological well-being. Depression, anxiety, and psychological stress are the most commonly reported concerns, though prevalence estimates vary substantially. While some interventions exist, they are narrow in scope and lack evidence for effectiveness at scale. Factors associated with variation in mental health and psychological wellbeing among CIS include academic stress, social isolation, language difficulties, cultural adjustment, and inadequate institutional support.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: High-quality evidence on prevalence and intervention effectiveness remains limited. These findings underscore the need for more robust, culturally responsive support systems and interventions to address the mental health needs of CIS in Western higher education settings.

items.title: Alcohol-Related Health Disorders: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Nishikawa H, Asai A, Kim SK, Yoshio S.

sections.text: There is a theory that light drinking is good for health and can extend lifespan compared to those who do not drink. However, a 2018 WHO report showed that, when considering the burden of disease-which includes not only deaths but also general health impairments-zero alcohol consumption is the safest option, and that the burden of disease increases as alcohol consumption rises. The theory that light or moderate drinking is good for health is increasingly being refuted. Alcohol consumption is the cause of a wide range of diseases, including liver damage, metabolic disorders, cardiovascular diseases, malignancies, and sarcopenia. From a health economics perspective, alcohol consumption, which increases the risk of lifestyle-related diseases, also affects labor productivity. It is estimated that there are more than 10 million habitual drinkers in Japan whose drinking habits increase their risk of lifestyle-related diseases, and more than 1 million people with alcohol use disorder (scoring 20 or higher on the Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test). However, the reality is that only about 50,000 Japanese people with alcohol use disorder actually receive treatment. This indicates that interventions for alcohol dependence in Japan are inadequate. This narrative review paper overviews recent topics of alcohol-related health disorders.

items.title: Maladaptive state allocation: an orexin-based framework linking sleep disturbance, chronic pain, and substance use disorder.
items.authors: Brunson KE, Bellitire SC, Kuper SD, Alcala ACE, Martin-Fardon R, Flores-Ramirez FJ.

sections.text: Sleep disturbance, chronic pain, and substance use disorders are highly prevalent conditions that frequently co-occur and exacerbate one another. Although traditionally studied as distinct clinical entities, growing evidence suggests they share common neurobiological mechanisms. Among these, the orexin (OX; also known as hypocretin) system has emerged as a critical regulator of arousal, motivation, stress responsiveness, and nociception, positioning it as a potential contributor to interactions among sleep, pain, and addiction. In this review, we propose that OX may function as a state-integration network that coordinates behavioral responses to competing physiological and environmental demands. Through widespread projections to brainstem, thalamic, limbic, and mesolimbic circuits, OX transmission dynamically regulates vigilance, salience attribution, pain modulation, and reward-seeking behavior. Under physiological conditions, these actions promote adaptive behavioral prioritization. However, chronic dysregulation of OX transmission may result in maladaptive state allocation characterized by persistent hyperarousal, amplified pain-related salience, and excessive motivational value assigned to drug-associated cues. We synthesize experimental evidence implicating OX-dependent circuits in the pathophysiology of sleep disturbance, chronic pain, and substance use disorder and introduce a conceptual triad model linking these conditions. Within this framework, we propose that sleep loss may increase pain sensitivity and craving, chronic pain may disrupt sleep and promote substance use, and repeated drug exposure may further destabilize sleep and pain regulation, creating a self-reinforcing cycle. Finally, we discuss individual factors that may influence vulnerability to triadic comorbidity and highlight emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the OX system.

items.title: Perceived stress, occupational burnout, and anxiety among PIVAS healthcare professionals: the moderating role of research competence.
items.authors: Chen Q, Yang C, Yang L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Pharmacy Intravenous Admixture Services (PIVAS) are now an integral part of patient care in modern hospitals. However, personnel working in PIVAS are often exposed to intense perceived stress, making them more susceptible to occupational burnout and anxiety, which may negatively impact their physical and mental health, as well as job performance. This study aims to explore the relationships between perceived stress, occupational burnout, research competence, and anxiety.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among PIVAS nurses and pharmacists from hospitals. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire that included sociodemographic information, work experience, perceived stress, and related psychological parameters. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to examine the hypothesized direct and indirect relationships among perceived stress, occupational burnout, and anxiety, and to assess the moderating role of research competence.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 609 healthcare professionals from 137 medical institutions in 20 provinces across China participated in the analysis, including 61.6% (375/609) nurses and 38.4% (234/609) pharmacists. 40.9% of participants exhibited symptoms of anxiety. SEM analysis revealed that perceived stress was significantly and positively associated with occupational burnout (z = 6.08, p < 0.05) and anxiety (z = 7.59, p < 0.05), with burnout showing direct and indirect effects within the hypothesized model. Moreover, research competence acted as a positive moderator in the relationships between perceived stress and occupational burnout, perceived stress and anxiety, as well as burnout and anxiety.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Occupational burnout, anxiety, and perceived stress are common among PIVAS nurses and pharmacists. The findings highlight that perceived stress is significantly associated with higher levels of burnout and anxiety symptoms. Notably, research competence moderated these associations. Healthcare institutions should prioritize effective stress management strategies, enhance employees' research competence, and provide psychological support to mitigate the association between perceived stress and mental health. Future studies should explore the causal relationships between these variables and investigate targeted intervention approaches.

SEM analysis revealed that perceived stress was significantly and positively associated with occupational burnout (z = 6.08, p < 0.05) and anxiety (z = 7.59, p < 0.05), with burnout showing direct and indirect effects within the hypothesized model. Moreover, research competence acted as a positive moderator in the relationships between perceived stress and occupational burnout, perceived stress and anxiety, as well as burnout and anxiety.

Occupational burnout, anxiety, and perceived stress are common among PIVAS nurses and pharmacists. Healthcare institutions should prioritize effective stress management strategies, enhance employees' research competence, and provide psychological support to mitigate the association between perceived stress and mental health. Future studies should explore the causal relationships between these variables and investigate targeted intervention approaches.

items.title: Post-TAVI Hypotension as a Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenge: A Case Report of Delayed-Onset Suicide Left Ventricle.
items.authors: Pepe M, Barnaba I, Caretto P, Mastrangelo A, Moretti M, Giordano S, Tritto R, Ciccone MM.
items.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis leads to haemodynamic improvement. Patients with a small, hypertrophic left ventricle are predisposed to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO). Abrupt afterload reduction may trigger "suicide left ventricle", characterised by hypercontractility, near-complete cavity obliteration, systolic anterior motion (SAM)-related LVOTO, and hypotension. Early recognition is crucial because treatments may aggravate the obstruction.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: A 78-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidaemia, severe calcific tricuspid aortic stenosis, LV hypertrophy, small LV cavity, and bifascicular block underwent pre-TAVI evaluation. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary disease; because of recurrent syncope, a dual-chamber pacemaker was implanted before TAVI. After transfemoral implantation of a 29 mm Medtronic Evolut FX+ bioprosthesis, the patient developed dyspnoea and hypotension. Bleeding, arrhythmias, and cardiac tamponade were excluded, and no evidence of an acute structural prosthetic complication was identified. Echocardiography showed SAM, a hyperdynamic LV with near-complete systolic cavity obliteration, and a 106 mmHg LVOT gradient with a "dagger-shaped" profile. Intravenous fluid administration, avoidance of diuretics, esmolol, and pacemaker reprogramming were followed by haemodynamic stabilisation and a reduction in LVOTO.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Suicide left ventricle is a rare cause of post-TAVI hypotension; male sex and delayed haemodynamic instability were atypical. Early echocardiographic recognition, post-procedural monitoring, and pathophysiology-driven management were paramount for preventing progression to shock.

items.title: The Insomnia Daytime Symptoms and Impacts Questionnaire: a qualitative interview study of content validity in insomnia disorder and comorbid conditions.
items.authors: Phillips Beyer A, Pepin JL, Kimel M, Kirk K, Trimble DG, Vaillant C, Olivieri A, Dauvilliers Y.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: The Insomnia Daytime Symptoms and Impacts Questionnaire (IDSIQ) is a 14-item patient-reported outcome (PRO) measure evaluating the effects of insomnia disorder on daytime functioning. Previous validation work for the IDSIQ did not include patients with known comorbidities such as alcohol use disorder (AUD), obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and mild cognitive impairment due to probable Alzheimer's disease (MCI-AD), which often underlie or contribute to insomnia.

sections.heading: Patients and methods
sections.text: We conducted cross-sectional qualitative interview studies in US adults with self-reported insomnia and comorbid AUD, OSA, or MCI-AD. Concept elicitation interviews and cognitive debriefing interviews were conducted, the latter after participants completed the IDSIQ electronically. Qualitative data were analyzed by content analysis and quantitative data through calculation of descriptive statistics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Ten participants with AUD, 20 with OSA, and 15 with MCI-AD completed interviews. Participants reported that insomnia had physical, emotional, cognitive, work-related, and social impacts and affected their ability to do daily activities. Most participants found the IDSIQ relevant to their experiences, clear, understandable, and of acceptable length. Most participants understood the response options and considered both the options and the recall period of "today" appropriate. While individual participants suggested possible changes to the IDSIQ, none of the suggestions emerged consistently such that changes to the IDSIQ seemed to be warranted.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study provides qualitative evidence supporting content validity of the IDSIQ in patients with insomnia and three comorbidities. The results indicate that the IDSIQ can be used for clinical research in patients with insomnia and three frequently associated comorbidities.

items.title: The relationship between mental health and academic performance amongst undergraduate medical students in low-middle income countries (LMICs): a protocol for a systematic review.
items.authors: Gumede A, Tendamudzimu M, Ramoroka K, Buthelezi N, Mantse S, Mphago R, Thobejane K, Lentoor A.

sections.text: Globally, mental health disorders such as depression, stress, and anxiety are prevalent amongst undergraduate medical students, which may negatively impact their academic performance. In low-middle-income settings (LIMCs), where academic expectations are significant with limited mental health resources, this link necessitates further investigations. The protocol outlines a systematic review to synthesize evidence on the link between mental health status and academic outcomes amongst undergraduate medical students in LMICs. The systematic review will be conducted and reported in line with the JBI methodology and PRISMA 2020 guiding statement. A comprehensive electronic literature database search, namely Scopus, MEDLINE (PubMed), CINAHL, and Google Scholar, will be carried out using Medical Search Terms (MeSH) for articles published within the past 10 years (January 2016-December 2026). The search and selection of relevant studies will be conducted by two independent reviewers, with 2 additional reviewers independently screening titles, abstracts, and full texts. Data will be independently extracted by all reviewers, and any conflicts arising during this process will be resolved through a fifth reviewer. The JBI Critical Appraisal Checklists will be used to evaluate bias. All included studies will be subjected to narrative thematic synthesis using NVivo software. The JBI ConQual approach will be used to evaluate the confidence of the synthesized findings, which incorporates dependability and credibility themes.

items.title: The systems mapping matrix: an educational framework based on complex adaptive systems for integrating contemporary psychiatric science into undergraduate medical education.
items.authors: Rodriguez Pulido F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Contemporary psychiatric science has evolved beyond reductionist models toward a multidimensional understanding of mental disorders that incorporates genetic vulnerability, epigenetic regulation, attachment, identity development, symptom networks, environmental adversity, recovery processes, and complexity science. Although these advances have transformed psychiatric knowledge, undergraduate medical education continues to rely predominantly on linear and categorical approaches. This review aimed to synthesize these developments within a Complex Adaptive Systems (CAS) perspective and to develop the Systems Mapping Matrix as an educational framework for undergraduate psychiatry. The Systems Mapping Matrix is an educational tool that maps and integrates multiple scientific domains into a coherent framework for clinical reasoning.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An integrative narrative review was conducted to synthesise evidence from eight complementary scientific domains relevant to undergraduate psychiatric education. Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science using predefined search strategies covering eight conceptual domains: psychiatric genetics, epigenetics, attachment, identity development, network psychopathology, stressful life events, meaning and recovery, and complexity science. Evidence was synthesized narratively to identify conceptual convergence and educational implications rather than quantitative effect estimates.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Ninety-six publications met the inclusion criteria. Despite their methodological diversity, the reviewed domains converged around core characteristics of Complex Adaptive Systems, including non-linearity, emergence, dynamic interactions, context dependence and adaptive change. This synthesis informed the development of the Systems Mapping Matrix, an educational framework that organizes contemporary psychiatric knowledge into an integrated systems perspective. The Matrix supports multilevel clinical reasoning, biopsychosocial formulation, systems thinking and person-centred decision-making while complementing, rather than replacing, conventional diagnostic models.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The Systems Mapping Matrix provides a theoretically grounded educational framework for translating contemporary psychiatric science into undergraduate medical education. By integrating multiple scientific domains through the principles of Complex Adaptive Systems, it may facilitate the development of adaptive clinical reasoning and a more holistic understanding of mental disorders. Future research should evaluate its educational effectiveness and impact on learning outcomes.

items.title: Delirium as a marker of systemic vulnerability in hospitalized patients with COVID-19: a multicenter cohort study with extended follow-up.
items.authors: Cho S, Han S, Hong A, Jang Y, Song KH, Choe PG, Park HY, Park HY.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Delirium is a common neuropsychiatric complication in hospitalized patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and has been linked to short-term mortality. However, its long-term prognostic significance and whether it independently contributes to death remain unclear. This multicenter cohort study aimed to identify the risk factors for delirium and evaluate their prognostic significance.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective cohort study included 1,030 patients with COVID-19 at two tertiary hospitals in Seoul and Gyeonggi-do, South Korea (January 2021 to December 2022), excluding those with prior dementia. Delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method and diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria. Logistic regression was used to identify the risk factors for delirium. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression were used to evaluate survival.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 1,030 patients (mean age 62.9 years, 44.4% women), 119 (11.6%) developed delirium and 264 (25.8%) died. Mortality was significantly higher in the delirium group (47.1% vs. 23.0%, p < 0.001). Independent risk factors for delirium were advanced age (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.05), higher COVID-19 severity (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.56-4.53), and pre-admission antipsychotic use (OR 3.52, 95% CI 1.44-8.63). Unadjusted survival was shorter in the delirium group (18.0 vs. 25.6 months, p < 0.001), but after multivariable adjustment, delirium did not independently predict mortality (HR 1.33, 95% CI 0.89-2.00, p = 0.16). Mortality was significantly associated with older age, comorbidity burden, COVID-19 severity, and the use of opioids and antiepileptic medication.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Delirium reflects systemic vulnerability rather than being a direct determinant of mortality. Early identification and proactive management of patients at high risk of delirium may improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: A systematic review of school-based mental health and wellbeing interventions for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students in Australia (2015-2024).
items.authors: Malik N, Butler T, Garvey D, Anderson K.

sections.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander young people's wellbeing is grounded in culture, identity, and connection to community and Country. Schools offer unique opportunities to support wellbeing through culturally safe environments, trusted relationships, and community partnerships. Despite a range of school-based wellbeing programs, there has been a lack of comprehensive reporting and synthesis of existing programs.This review synthesised peer-reviewed and grey literature to identify Australian school-based wellbeing programs for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students and examined design, delivery, and reported outcomes. Database searches identified 1,853 records; 71 studies met inclusion criteria. Primary school programs emphasised culture through play-based and physical activities. Secondary programs targeted mental health, academic engagement, and leadership. Remote programs centred on culture and language; urban programs addressed broader wellbeing domains.Cultural grounding, relationships, community participation, and holistic design were the key features most commonly reported across programs associated with positive outcomes. Most evaluations reported favourable findings; however, confidence in these findings is limited by heterogeneous evaluation designs, an absence of comparison groups, reliance on self-reported and practice-based assessment, inconsistent outcome measurement, and limited longitudinal follow-up. No formal quality appraisal was undertaken, and this review therefore describes features of promising programs rather than establishing intervention effectiveness.

items.title: Psychotropic drug-induced lipid disturbances: a genome-wide association study in a Swiss psychiatric cohort.
items.authors: Jan M, Delacrétaz A, Dubath C, Guex N, Gamma F, Preisig M, Crettol Wavre S, Ansermot N, Vandenberghe F, Grandjean C, Plessen KJ, von Gunten A, Conus P, Kutalik Z, Eap CB.

sections.text: Dyslipidemia affects patients with severe mental illness to varying degrees, partly due to medication side effects and genetic variations that modify drug-induced lipid changes. To identify these genetics contributors, we conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) on 829 patients of the PsyMetab cohort whose total-, LDL-, HDL- cholesterol and triglyceride levels were recorded pre- and up to one-year post psychotropic treatment. Seven different loci were associated at genome wide significance level (P < 5 × 10^-8) with treatment-induced lipids changes. Three genetic variants were associated with total cholesterol change following aripiprazole, quetiapine, and combination of quetiapine, olanzapine, clozapine treatment (rs17313064 G > A, rs12543987 G > A, rs58331124 G > A, respectively). Two markers were associated with HDL-cholesterol change following lithium and mirtazapine treatment (rs12097296 C > T, rs10933971 C > T, respectively). One variant was associated with triglycerides change following risperidone treatment (rs10260518 G > T) and finally one genetic variation was associated with triglycerides change considering any drug treatment (rs56286230 T > G). To compensate for the lack of classical replication, sensitivity analyses were conducted by assessing the robustness of effects using different post-treatment interval lengths. Notably rs10933971 effect on HLD-cholesterol was consistently found across different patients and time-frames. These findings point to genes previously associated with total lipids level in the general population and highlight novel drug-specific associations which provide promising insights toward personalized psychotropic therapy.

items.title: High-Quality Genome Assembly and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveal Potential Pathways for Psilocybin Biosynthesis in Gymnopilus dilepis.
items.authors: Yao S, Liu Y, Xia W, Xia Y, Yang K, Li H, Xie B.

sections.text: Psilocybin has demonstrated efficacy in the treatment of mental health conditions, including anxiety and depression. It is evident that G. dilepis possesses the capacity to produce psilocybin. Therefore, conducting in-depth research into this species will contribute to the understanding of the biosynthetic mechanisms of psilocybin and provide a more comprehensive insight into its biosynthesis. We have assembled the G. dilepis genome at the chromosomal level. G. dilepis is characterized by a chromosome number of 13, a genome size of 54.2 Mb, and a total of 15,211 predicted genes and 16,411,190 transposable elements. The evolutionary analysis suggests that G. dilepis can produce psilocybin due to its close relationship with the Psilocybe genus of mushrooms. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis revealed that the biosynthesis of psilocybin is associated with several amino acid metabolic pathways, particularly those involving cysteine and methionine metabolism, arginine and proline metabolism, and tryptophan metabolism. These pathways may supply the precursor substances required for psilocybin biosynthesis. This study presents a high-quality genome assembly for G. dilepis and reveals a close relationship between amino acid metabolism and psilocybin biosynthesis, providing a theoretical basis for exploring the genetic relationships in G. dilepis and the genes that regulate the biosynthesis of psilocybin.

items.title: Associations of social determinants of health, allostatic load, and brain age gaps in adolescence.
items.authors: Yang Y, Liu J, Yu L, Li H, Kong T, Ji F, Zhang X, Gong G, Liu R, Luo L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Social determinants of health (SDOH) are fundamental drivers of behavioral outcomes; however, their impact on adolescents' brain age gap (BAG)-an integrated neural marker reflecting deviations from normative brain maturation and potential brain plasticity-remain poorly understood. Moreover, the biological mechanisms underlying the effects are unknown.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a prospective cohort analysis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (T1: n = 7330, 46.9% female, 55.2% White; diffusion tensor imaging (DTI): n = 6963, 46.7% female, 55.9% White; resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI): n = 6482, 47.3% female, 56.3% White; multimodal MRI: n = 6334, 47.2% female, 56.7% White), and applied XGBoost regression models to estimate T1, DTI, rs-fMRI, and multimodal BAGs, separately. We then used Bayesian multilevel models to examine the associations among SDOH, BAG, allostatic load, lifestyle factors, and mental health phenotypes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We found that positive SDOH (e.g., reduced exposure to industrial pollutants, high educational quality, and socioeconomic advantages) were associated with smaller BAGs, which indicate promoted brain plasticity; negative SDOH (e.g., number of early childhood education centers, unemployment rate, sexism, and racism) were associated with larger BAGs, which reflect lower brain plasticity. Allostatic load mediated the associations between SDOH and BAGs. Adequate nutritional intake amplified the effects of regional educational attainment on enhancing brain plasticity through reduced allostatic load. Only the larger rs-fMRI BAG predicted increased depression two years later.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings underscore the critical roles of SDOH in shaping brain aging and highlight allostatic load as a key intervention target for promoting optimal brain development and mental health.

Social determinants of health (SDOH) are fundamental drivers of behavioral outcomes; however, their impact on adolescents' brain age gap (BAG)-an integrated neural marker reflecting deviations from normative brain maturation and potential brain plasticity-remain poorly understood. We conducted a prospective cohort analysis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (T1: n = 7330, 46.9% female, 55.2% White; diffusion tensor imaging (DTI): n = 6963, 46.7% female, 55.9% White; resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI): n = 6482, 47.3% female, 56.3% White; multimodal MRI: n = 6334, 47.2% female, 56.7% White), and applied XGBoost regression models to estimate T1, DTI, rs-fMRI, and multimodal BAGs, separately. We then used Bayesian multilevel models to examine the associations among SDOH, BAG, allostatic load, lifestyle factors, and mental health phenotypes.

We found that positive SDOH (e.g., reduced exposure to industrial pollutants, high educational quality, and socioeconomic advantages) were associated with smaller BAGs, which indicate promoted brain plasticity; negative SDOH (e.g., number of early childhood education centers, unemployment rate, sexism, and racism) were associated with larger BAGs, which reflect lower brain plasticity. Allostatic load mediated the associations between SDOH and BAGs. Adequate nutritional intake amplified the effects of regional educational attainment on enhancing brain plasticity through reduced allostatic load. Only the larger rs-fMRI BAG predicted increased depression two years later.

These findings underscore the critical roles of SDOH in shaping brain aging and highlight allostatic load as a key intervention target for promoting optimal brain development and mental health.

items.title: Predictors of 30-day pulmonary readmissions in patients with COPD: a case-control study.
items.authors: Wehbeh BED, Itani M, Ghassani H, Kaady T, Salameh R, Bazzi J, Boufakhreddine H, Bouakl I.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations account for substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare expenditure worldwide. Thirty-day readmission for respiratory causes represents a critical quality outcome that reflects the adequacy of acute management and post-discharge care. Data from the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) remain scarce.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective unmatched case-control study at the American University of Beirut Medical Center (AUBMC), Lebanon (January 2019-August 2025). Cases (n = 150) were patients readmitted within 30 days of discharge for a respiratory cause following an index COPD exacerbation admission. Controls (n = 202) were patients not readmitted for a respiratory cause within 30 days. Univariate and multivariable binary logistic regression were used to identify independent predictors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In the primary multivariable model (n = 135), blood eosinophil count ≥ 300 cells/µL was the strongest independent risk factor for readmission (aOR 38.01, 95% CI 3.51-411.9; p = 0.003), followed by antidepressant use (aOR 4.61, 95% CI 1.28-16.62; p = 0.020) and lower FEV1 (aOR 0.93 per 1%, 95% CI 0.89-0.98; p = 0.005). Inhaler step-up at discharge was the strongest independent protective predictor (aOR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01-0.39; p = 0.003), followed by post-discharge follow-up attendance (aOR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03-0.79; p = 0.025). Key findings were replicated in a sensitivity analysis in the full cohort.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Inhaler step-up at discharge and post-discharge follow-up are the strongest modifiable protective factors against 30-day respiratory readmission. Blood eosinophilia identifies a high-risk phenotype specifically prone to recurrent obstructive exacerbations and may represent a target for ICS-guided discharge prescribing. Psychiatric comorbidity is an independent readmission driver not explained by disease severity. A structured discharge bundle of care incorporating these modifiable elements needs prospective validation.

items.title: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors in Atherosclerosis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Impact-A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Mozaffari S, Dehghan Banadaki A, Sanjari Pirayvatloo P, Shamohammadi MS, Haraj A, Hoseini D, Bahri AM, Nazari MA, Kachuei M.

sections.text: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the arterial wall characterized by endothelial dysfunction, lipid accumulation, and immune activation. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), widely prescribed for depression and anxiety disorders, inhibit the serotonin transporter, and it has been proposed that they influence atherosclerosis through serotonin-dependent and other mechanisms. This narrative review examines whether SSRIs modify atherosclerosis-related pathways, including inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial function, lipid handling, and platelet activity, and how these observations compare with clinical cardiovascular findings. English-language literature was identified through nonsystematic searches of PubMed and Google Scholar (last search: August 2025), supplemented by targeted searches during revision. Preclinical findings are mixed: Some cell-based and animal studies suggest reduced endothelial adhesion-molecule expression, inflammatory cytokine production, and oxidative stress, whereas studies that directly quantified lesions found greater atherosclerosis with fluoxetine in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice and with sertraline in female cynomolgus monkeys. Clinical evidence must be interpreted according to endpoint type because direct plaque measures, surrogate vascular markers, thrombotic events, and nonatherosclerotic cardiac outcomes yield different signals. Observational associations with lower event rates are vulnerable to confounding by indication, and randomized trials designed primarily to assess psychiatric efficacy and safety have not demonstrated cardiovascular benefit. Individual SSRIs differ in pharmacokinetics, cytochrome P450 inhibition, and QT liability, and their shared antiplatelet action increases bleeding risk, particularly with concomitant antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Vascular effects of SSRIs are biologically plausible, but this plausibility has not been matched by consistent evidence of reduced atherosclerosis in humans. No indication currently exists for the use of SSRIs as antiatherosclerotic therapy, and longitudinal studies with clearly differentiated endpoints are needed to determine whether any causal effect exists.
