items.title: Regression Analysis of the Relationship Between Neurogenesis and Maze Learning in Rats with Divergent Behavioral Phenotypes.
items.authors: Nedogreeva O, Mamedova D, Riga V, Aniol V, Lazareva N, Gulyaeva N, Stepanichev M.

sections.text: The relationship between learning capacity and hippocampal neurogenesis is still poorly understood. Moreover, the effect of pathological behavior on this relationship is unknown. In this study, we investigated this problem in rats with different behavioral phenotypes. Wistar-Kyoto rats were used as a model for depression, and Spontaneous Hypertensive rats (SHRs) were used to model attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Normotensive Wistar rats (NWR) served as a standard behavioral control. We trained rats in the Barnes maze and then assessed their cognitive flexibility. We estimated the density of doublecortin-expressing neural precursors in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus dentate gyrus, and, finally, we applied regression analysis to study the relationship between learning indices and the DCX+ cell density. It was shown that SHRs exhibited poorer performance during the maze training, and WKY rats displayed the lowest learning efficiency. In NWRs and SHRs, learning did not correlate with ongoing neurogenesis, probably due to different biological substrates. In WKY rats, a strong inverse correlation was found between DCX+ cell density in the dentate gyrus and learning efficiency during training and reversed training sessions. These findings suggest that cognitive deficits in WKY are predominantly hippocampus-dependent, while cognitive problems in SHRs are primarily driven by dysfunction of other brain structures and impaired executive control.

items.title: Psychotropic Polypharmacy Discontinuation Patterns in Youth.
items.authors: Hughes PM, Annis IE, Cao Y, Jackson KD, deJong NA, Christian RB, Davis SA, Thomas KC.

sections.text: The objective of this study was to document psychotropic polypharmacy discontinuation among several common medication pairs with drug-drug interaction potential (DDIP) among medically complex children. We identified 12 commonly prescribed psychotropic DDIP pairs based on pharmacology and clinical expertise. Using North Carolina Medicaid claims (2011-2022), we constructed a cohort of children receiving each DDIP pair (n = 639-20,683). For each cohort, we described cohort demographics (age, sex, rurality, mental, and physical diagnoses), which drug in the pair was initiated first, which was discontinued first, and the time until discontinuation. Using the Kaplan-Meier method, we documented the probability of persisting on each DDIP pair at 30, 90, 180, and 365 days. The demographic profile of each DDIP pair varied, with the amitriptyline and fluoxetine pair having notable differences in nearly all categories. Over 90% of patients discontinued each DDIP pair by 365 days, with median times to discontinuation ranging from 75 to 111 days. Most pairs had a relatively even distribution of which drug in the pair was initiated and discontinued first; however, amitriptyline and olanzapine were both discontinued first for over half of their respective DDIP cohorts. The amitriptyline and fluoxetine pair also had the lowest probability of persistence at 365 days (10.2%). In a cohort of medically complex children, two DDIP pairs appear to warrant future research: (1) amitriptyline and fluoxetine and (2) fluoxetine and olanzapine. Both pairs showed frequent discontinuation, and the demographics of children using the amitriptyline and fluoxetine pair were markedly different from other pairs without clinical explanations.

items.title: A Dynamic, Inflammation-Aware Framework for Safe Clozapine Prescribing in East Asian Populations.
items.authors: Nagamine T.

sections.text: Background: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, yet it remains underused in many East Asian settings. Lower average dose requirements have often been attributed to CYP1A2 genetic variation, but genotype alone does not adequately explain interindividual or within-patient variability. Methods: This narrative review synthesises targeted literature on clozapine pharmacokinetics, CYP1A2 regulation, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), inflammation and clinically important adverse effects. Results: Clozapine exposure reflects both relatively stable characteristics and time-varying factors, including smoking, interacting medicines, adherence and inflammatory illness. Cytokine-mediated CYP1A2 suppression provides a plausible mechanism for concentration increases during inflammation, although the causal contribution and direction of the proposed feedback relationship require prospective study. The review presents a conceptual, three-phase framework for integrating clinical assessment, inflammatory markers and TDM, with attention to metabolic, respiratory, gastrointestinal and haematological risks. The framework is not a validated dosing algorithm and does not replace established guidance or mandatory blood-monitoring programmes. Conclusions: This framework offers a testable approach to longitudinal clozapine assessment in East Asian populations; its clinical utility and generalisability require external prospective validation.

items.title: Association of workplace age discrimination with health-related quality of life among young- to middle-aged primary and secondary school teachers in Taiwan: Roles of loneliness, life satisfaction, and psychological distress.
items.authors: Saffari M, Huang PC, Lin CY, Lin WT, Üztemur S, Chen IH, Griffiths MD, Chang YH.
items.journal: Health and quality of life outcomes

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Workplace age discrimination (WAD) is an emerging psychosocial stressor that may undermine health-related quality of life (HRQoL), including those working in educational settings. The present study examined associations between WAD and HRQoL and tested potential mediators among Taiwanese schoolteachers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In a cross-sectional online survey, 611 teachers (75% female; mean age 40.9 ± 9.9 years) completed measures of WAD, depression/anxiety/stress (DASS-21), life satisfaction, loneliness (3-item UCLA Loneliness Scale), and HRQoL (WHOQOL-BREF). Pearson correlations and Hayes' PROCESS (Model 4; 5,000 bootstraps) were used.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: All variables were significantly intercorrelated (r = - 0.588 to 0.709, all p-values < 0.001). Higher WAD was directly associated with (i) poorer physical, social, and environmental HRQoL, but not psychological HRQoL, (ii) lower life satisfaction, (iii) greater psychological distress, and (iv) greater loneliness (all p-values < 0.001). Significant indirect associations between WAD and all four HRQoL domains were observed through psychological distress and life satisfaction, while loneliness showed significant indirect associations with physical, psychological and social HRQoL but not environmental HRQoL (β = -0.12 to - 0.01). Therefore, although the direct association between WAD and psychological HRQoL was non-significant, significant indirect associations were evident through all three psychosocial variables.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: WAD relates to poorer HRQoL largely through psychological distress, loneliness, and reduced life satisfaction. Targeting these factors may mitigate WAD's impact among Taiwanese teachers.

items.title: Promoting help-seeking using e-technology for adolescents with mental health problems: Results from a RCT within the ProHEAD Consortium.
items.authors: Kaess M, Cavelti M, Sele S, Lustig S, Moessner M, Bauer S, Becker K, Thomasius R, Rummel-Kluge C, Eschenbeck H, Hiery A, Kohls E, Lehner L, Koenig J, ProHEAD Consortium.

sections.text: Mental health problems (MHP) are common in adolescents. Help-seeking behavior (HSB) in this age group is low. An online intervention promoting HSB in adolescents with MHP (ProHEAD-Online) was evaluated in a randomized controlled trial. It was hypothesized that adolescents allocated to ProHEAD-Online would show increased real-world HSB after 12 months compared to adolescents in the control group. A multicenter randomized controlled trial was conducted in a school-based community setting in Germany. n = 1470 students (≥12 years, 74.6% female) with MHP and no HSB at baseline were randomized (ProHEAD-Online: n = 739; control: n = 731). Professional HSB of 4.5% (control) and 5.7% (ProHEAD-Online) was reported at the primary endpoint (OR = 1.27, 95% CI = [0.78, 2.10], p = 0.34). Age at baseline moderated the treatment effect (OR = 0.79, 95% CI = [0.64, 0.97], p = 0.03), ProHEAD-Online only improved HSB in younger adolescents. No significant differences by treatment arm on secondary outcomes (i.e., severity of MHP, health-related quality of life, attitudes toward help-seeking, perceived barriers to help-seeking, help-seeking intentions, and treatment satisfaction). Professional HSB in adolescents with MHP is low. An online intervention to increase HSB in adolescents with MHP was not superior to static online content. Improving HSB, particularly among older adolescents, remains challenging.

items.title: Proteomic predictors of serum anti-müllerian hormone levels.
items.authors: Valenti M, Huang K, Liu Y, Yang AR, Olson M, Hlomatchi FJ, Hollister J, Kolar JJ, Stea D, Beitel SC, Craig ZR, Furlong M, Burgess JL, Farland LV.

sections.text: Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), a marker of ovarian reserve, is associated with time to menopause, fertility, and certain adverse gynecologic conditions. Few studies have evaluated proteins associated with AMH levels. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to use an untargeted proteomic wide association analysis to identify proteins associated with serum AMH levels. A sample of women firefighters enrolled in the Fire Fighter Cancer Cohort Study were included in the analysis ( n  = 142). Serum samples were sent for proteomic and AMH analysis. Linear regression models estimating the association of AMH with untargeted proteomics were conducted adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI) (continuous), race, firefighter status, region, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) diagnosis. A pathway analysis using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) was conducted to identify statistically significantly enriched pathways associated with AMH outcomes using effective size-ranked protein sets. The analysis was performed using the gseGO and gseKEGG functions in the R package clusterProfiler for Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) databases, respectively. The average age of participants was 34.1 years (6.2 SD), with the majority being white (83.9%) non-Hispanic (82.8%). Ten proteins (TENM4, SIRT6, AZIN1, NCR3, CGA|FSHB, TPSG1, TNFRSF14, ADAM11, TSSK2, IL22RA1) were observed to be inversely associated with AMH and one protein (BTD) was positively associated with AMH. CGA|FSHB is involved in ovarian follicle development and regulation. TSSK2 has recently been identified in mouse ovarian follicles. TENM4, SIRT6, AZIN1, IL-22RA1 are associated with ovarian function. NCR3, TPSG1, TNFRSF14, and ADAM11 are involved in immune function. BTD plays a role in the regulation of gene expression. Pathways involved in hormone regulation, immune signaling, and metabolic activity were significantly enriched. Our study identified previously known (CGA|FSHB ) and novel proteomic associations with serum AMH levels. These findings provide insight into protein and biological pathways associated with AMH levels. Further research among a larger sample is needed to corroborate these findings.

items.title: Sex Differences in Psychological Traits, Training Volume, and Dietary Food-Frequency Patterns in Athletes: Associations with Body Dissatisfaction.
items.authors: Ramírez-Goercke MI, Yáñez-Sepúlveda R, Giakoni-Ramírez F, Clemente-Suárez VJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychological traits, training volume, and dietary behaviors have been associated with body-image and eating-related outcomes in athletes, but evidence integrating these domains from a sex-based perspective remains limited.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study examined sex differences in psychological traits, weekly training volume, and study-specific dietary food-frequency scores, and evaluated their associations with body dissatisfaction assessed using the Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the Eating Disorder Inventory (EDI).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 58 athletes (23 women and 35 men). Participants completed questionnaires assessing personality traits, psychological inflexibility, anxiety, loneliness, training characteristics, dietary food-frequency patterns, and body dissatisfaction. Weekly training volume was calculated as the sum of weekly minutes across three intensity zones (Z1 + Z2 + Z3). Analyses included descriptive statistics, Welch's t -tests, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and a hypothesis-driven multivariable ordinary least squares model.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Female athletes had higher EDI Body Dissatisfaction scores and neuroticism than male athletes. Female athletes also had a higher non-pro-inflammatory food-frequency score (22.83 ± 6.31 vs. 19.34 ± 5.50; p = 0.036), whereas the pro-inflammatory food-frequency score did not differ significantly by sex ( p = 0.327). In the multivariable model, female sex (B = 2.615, p = 0.036) and the pro-inflammatory food-frequency score (B = 0.308, p = 0.048) were positively associated with EDI Body Dissatisfaction scores; BMI showed an imprecise positive estimate in both the primary and age-adjusted models, whereas neuroticism, weekly training volume, and the non-pro-inflammatory food-frequency score were not independently associated. Model fit was modest (adjusted R^2 = 0.180; 5-fold cross-validated R^2 = 0.058 ± 0.333).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Women in this sample reported greater body dissatisfaction and neuroticism. The association between the study-specific pro-inflammatory food-frequency score and body dissatisfaction was small and exploratory and should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal dietary effect or of biological inflammatory exposure. Larger studies with sport-type information, validated dietary indices, and objective training-load measures are required to test these associations.

items.title: Advances in transcranial alternating current stimulation and temporal interference stimulation for neuropsychiatric disorders: mechanisms, technical developments, and preclinical evidence.
items.authors: Wang Y, Chen L, Xie H, Wang C, Zhou D, Li X, Zhang J.

sections.text: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique that modulates neural activity through frequency- and phase-dependent electrical currents and has shown potential for enhancing cognition and alleviating symptoms in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Temporal interference (TI) stimulation applies two or more kilohertz-frequency electric fields with slightly different frequencies to generate a low-frequency amplitude-modulated field within neural tissue, offering a potential strategy for preferentially engaging deeper neural targets with improved spatial steering. Foundational studies in this field have used diverse methodologies, including multiscale computational modeling, cellular experiments, intact-animal studies, and disease-specific animal models, to elucidate stimulation principles, parameter dependencies, neuromodulatory mechanisms, safety, and functional efficacy. This review synthesizes recent advances in the basic and preclinical research of tACS and TI, with an emphasis on biophysical and physiological mechanisms, safety evaluation, parameter optimization, technological developments, peripheral nerve applications, and therapeutic effects and associated mechanisms in animal disease models. Current evidence indicates that both approaches can influence neural function across membrane, cellular, circuit, network, synaptic, and behavioral levels. Although tACS has undergone extensive human and clinical investigation, transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) remains at an earlier stage of mechanistic and translational development. Further systematic studies are required to clarify direct and indirect stimulation mechanisms, long-term safety, dose-response relationships, target engagement, and protocol optimization, thereby facilitating the clinical translation of these techniques, particularly for individualized and precision neuromodulation of brain disorders.

items.title: Electrocution-Induced Brain Injury: Report of Unique MRI Findings.
items.authors: Agharazi M, Naini PT, Shams Y, Sheikhinia N, Najafi MA.

sections.text: Electrocution is a form of electrical injury resulting from accidental contact with an electrical source, leading to potentially severe injuries across various organ systems, including the brain. This case report describes a 30-year-old male with a history of seizures and borderline personality disorder who lost consciousness after an electrocution incident. On admission, he was drowsy, disoriented, and had reduced motor strength and impaired sensory responses. He also had extensive leg wounds and dark-colored urine, suggestive of rhabdomyolysis. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed bilateral signal hyperintensity in the globus pallidi on T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences, as well as diffusion restrictions in the centrum semiovale, corona radiata, internal capsule, and occipital subcortical white matter on diffusion-weighted imaging and apparent diffusion coefficient maps. A follow-up MRI 1 month later demonstrated resolution of these restrictions on T2/FLAIR sequences. These findings highlight the importance of MRI in recognizing and monitoring electrocution-related brain injuries, with significant implications for clinical care and future research.

items.title: The Red Berry and the Brain: Lycium barbarum Polysaccharides in Neuroprotection.
items.authors: Yang C, Dong EQ, Luo JN, Zhang MH, Cui D, Lv JH, Chang JL.

sections.text: Psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders continue to contribute significantly to disability and mortality worldwide, a situation exacerbated by the lack of effective treatments capable of altering the course of these diseases, which poses a huge challenge to public health on a global scale. Lycium barbarum polysaccharides (LBPs), the major active components of Lycium barbarum, have attracted increasing attention owing to their promising neuroprotective properties demonstrated in cellular and animal disease models. This review summarises existing research on the mechanisms by which LBPs exert therapeutic effects in various cellular and animal models of neurological conditions. More specifically, it highlights the role of LBPs in attenuating Parkinson's disease by modulating the nuclear factor erythroid 2/haem oxygenase-1 (Nrf2/HO-1) pathways and the reactive oxygen species and nitric oxide (ROS-NO) pathways, in alleviating Alzheimer's disease by reducing beta-amyloid (Aβ) accumulation, as well as in attenuating ischaemia-reperfusion injury by modulating the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and mitochondrial dynamics. Furthermore, this review explores the potential of LBPs in the treatment of depression, whilst emphasising the urgent need to expand mechanistic studies beyond the prevailing inflammatory hypothesis. Through an integrative analysis of these molecular targets and signalling networks, this review establishes a comprehensive theoretical framework, proposes future research directions, and provides a theoretical basis for the use of LBPs in the treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: Suspected Lynch Syndrome Presenting With Synchronous Endometrial and Sigmoid Colon Adenocarcinomas and an Incidental Giant Ovarian Fibrothecoma: A Case Report.
items.authors: Rafiei M, Behboudi B, Ameli F, Zeinalkhani F, Ashtari S, Zamani N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Synchronous endometrial and colorectal carcinomas warrant evaluation for Lynch syndrome; however, MLH1/PMS2 loss may reflect sporadic MLH1 promoter hypermethylation rather than a germline defect.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: A 63-year-old woman with schizophrenia presented with 10-15 years of intermittent vaginal spotting. Evaluation revealed endometrioid endometrial carcinoma, sigmoid adenocarcinoma, and a large adnexal mass. She underwent hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, lymph node dissection, left colectomy, omentectomy, and appendectomy. Final pathology confirmed FIGO grade 2 endometrioid carcinoma, sigmoid adenocarcinoma, and benign ovarian fibrothecoma. Endometrial immunohistochemistry showed loss of MLH1/PMS2 with retained MSH2/MSH6, raising suspicion for Lynch syndrome; however, the diagnosis remained unconfirmed. Further tumor-based molecular and germline evaluation was recommended.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of synchronous malignancies and the need to distinguish sporadic from hereditary mismatch-repair deficiency.

items.title: Is the Income Trajectory of Older Patients with Gastric Cancer Associated with Mood Disorders? A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study in South Korea.
items.authors: Lee WR, Son N, Son Y, Kim JA, Yoo KB, Han KT.

sections.text: Mood disorders, influenced by income level and health-related stressors, are particularly concerning in financially and socially vulnerable older patients with gastric cancer. This study aimed to determine the relationship between income trajectory patterns and mood disorders within 5 years of cancer diagnosis in this population. This retrospective cohort study analyzed National Health Insurance Service-Senior cohort data from 2002 to 2019, focusing on older patients diagnosed with gastric cancer between 2008 and 2014. A latent class trajectory model was used to categorize the patients into five groups based on their income change patterns 6 years prior to cancer diagnosis up to 1 year post-diagnosis. We then used a Cox proportional hazards model to evaluate the association between income trajectories and mood disorder incidence and conducted subgroup analyses. Among the 4059 participants, 667 (16.4%) developed mood disorders within 5 years of cancer diagnosis. Cox regression analyses revealed that compared to the "consistently highest" income group 6 years prior to cancer diagnosis up to 1 year post-diagnosis, both the "consistently lowest" (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.05-1.81) and "decrease" (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.15-1.95) groups had a significantly high risk of 5-year mood disorder incidence. Persistently low and declining income trajectories were associated with higher risks of mood disorders among older patients with gastric cancer. These findings support monitoring financial difficulties and mental health and strengthening links between cancer care, psychological support, and social support.

items.title: Systemic Health and Endodontic Disease Burden: Influence of Root Canal Treatment Quality on Endodontic Outcomes.
items.authors: Zuim K, Qian F, Masiero AV, Hogden C, Gomez M, Parolia A.

sections.text: Background: Systemic health conditions are increasingly prevalent among patients receiving endodontic care and may influence the burden of endodontic disease. This study evaluated the prevalence of systemic health conditions among patients undergoing root canal treatment (RCT), their association with endodontic disease characteristics, and the influence of radiographic quality of root canal treatment (QRCT) on endodontic outcomes (EOs). Methods: This retrospective study reviewed electronic records and radiographs of 2036 patients who underwent RCT by predoctoral students between January 2021 and December 2025. Follow-up data sufficient for EO assessment were available for 590 teeth. Variables included systemic health conditions, tooth type, preoperative periapical status, and QRCT parameters (obturation length, density, taper, coronal seal, and procedural errors). EOs were classified using predefined clinical and radiographic criteria. Associations were analyzed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum, χ^2, and Fisher exact tests and multivariable logistic regression (α = 0.05). A sensitivity analysis was restricted to follow-up ≥12 months. Results: Systemic health conditions were identified in 57.9% of the overall study population (N = 2036) and in 64.1% of patients with evaluable endodontic outcomes (N = 590). Among patients with evaluable outcomes, mental health disorders (40.3%), hypertension (20.8%), neurological disorders (11.4%), and diabetes mellitus (10.7%) were the most prevalent systemic conditions. Overall treatment success was 86.1%. An exploratory association between mental health disorders and dental caries was observed. Mental health disorders were significantly associated with the presence of dental caries (unadjusted p = 0.049). QRCT was significantly associated with endodontic outcomes ( p < 0.001), with higher success rates in teeth with satisfactory treatment quality (88.4%) than in those with unsatisfactory treatment quality (65.5%). After adjustment for age, gender, tooth type, follow-up duration, preoperative periapical lesion status, and systemic health status, satisfactory QRCT was associated with greater odds of successful outcome (adjusted OR = 3.44; 95% CI, 1.82-6.50; p < 0.001). Longer follow-up was associated with lower odds of success (adjusted OR per 12 months = 0.74; 95% CI, 0.61-0.90; p = 0.003). Conclusions: Systemic health conditions were highly prevalent among patients receiving RCT and were associated with selected disease characteristics. However, satisfactory QRCT was the factor most strongly associated with successful EOs after adjustment for relevant patient and clinical characteristics. Practical Implications: Although systemic health conditions should be considered during patient assessment and treatment planning, achieving high-quality root canal treatment remains critical for optimizing endodontic outcomes and supports continued emphasis on technical excellence in clinical practice and dental education.

items.title: Socioecological Correlates of Physical Activity Among Medical Students at a Not-for-Profit University in Morocco: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: El Kirat H, Serhier Z, Hajjioui A, Belouali R, El Adib AR, Belrhiti Z.

sections.text: Background and Objectives: Physical inactivity and sedentary lifestyles are increasingly common among medical students and pose risks to their physical and mental health. In Morocco, little research examines what influences physical activity (PA) among medical students, especially those in not-for-profit universities, where academic and social settings may affect PA in unique ways. This study aimed to measure PA levels and identify associated factors among medical students at a not-for-profit university in Morocco. Materials and Methods: We carried out an online cross-sectional study with medical students at a not-for-profit university in Morocco from March to April 2024. Students completed a self-administered questionnaire based on the socioecological model and using validated scales. We used descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multivariable regression analysis with Jamovi version 2.5.1.0. Results: A total of 310 medical students took part in the study. Of these, 64.9% were considered physically active and met WHO recommendations for physical activity. However, only 23.4% reached PA levels associated with additional health benefits. The analysis showed that higher self-efficacy was associated with lower PA levels, whereas self-regulation showed varying associations across regression models. Basic psychological needs were significantly correlated with PA, whereas social support showed no significant association. The negative links with self-efficacy and self-regulation could mean that students think they can be active but do not act on it. The lack of associations with social support might show that support from others has less impact in a demanding academic setting. Conclusions: While some correlates of physical activity in this study are similar to those found in other groups of medical students, this research points out unique patterns among students at a not-for-profit medical university in Morocco. The study is original because it shows that well-known psychosocial factors may operate differently across settings. The negative links between self-efficacy, self-regulation, and PA, along with the lack of effect from social support, question some common ideas about what influences PA. These results highlight the need to consider the specific academic and social environment of not-for-profit medical schools when planning interventions and suggest that strategies should be tailored to address both personal and social factors.

items.title: The impact of diagnostic timing on healthcare use: statistical trends among early- and later-diagnosed autistic youth.
items.authors: Andreasen S, McCrimmon A, Zwaigenbaum L, McMorris CA.
items.journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

sections.text: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting approximately 1 in 50 Canadian children, with increasing prevalence over the past two decades, males being diagnosed at a four to one ratio to females, and a growing trend of later diagnoses in childhood/adolescence. While receiving a diagnosis after age six years is associated with co-occurring mental health conditions, little is known about how diagnostic timing influences healthcare service use patterns.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study examined whether later-diagnosed Autistic youth access more psychiatric healthcare services than those diagnosed earlier.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants included 147 Autistic youth from a public pediatric diagnostic clinic affiliated with a major children's hospital (median age at assessment = 5.00 years; 24.49% female). Healthcare utilization data were obtained from the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System (NACRS), including various healthcare visits. Negative binomial regression analyses determined whether diagnostic timing predicted number of healthcare encounters with sex as a moderator.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Groups were comparable in size (54% early diagnosed) and sex distribution. Controlling for age, being diagnosed later in adolescence predicted 59% more psychiatric visits ( β  = 0.47, p  = .024). This effect was reduced and no longer statistically significant when sex was included as a moderator ( β  = 0.42, p  = .066).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Later-diagnosed Autistic youth used more psychiatric services; however, with an underpowered sample, we were not able to detect sex-related differences. These findings highlight how diagnostic timing is potentially associated with the mental well-being and healthcare usage of Autistic youth, underscoring the need for targeted supports following a later autism diagnosis.

items.title: Physical education motivational climate and body self-concept among Chinese primary and secondary students: the serial mediating effects of basic psychological needs satisfaction and exercise motivation.
items.authors: Li J.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Physical education (PE) is the one setting in which nearly every school-age child meets structured physical activity, yet little is known about how the motivational atmosphere of PE classes relates to how students see their own bodies. This study examined whether the perceived mastery motivational climate in PE is associated with body self-concept among Chinese primary and secondary students, and whether basic psychological needs satisfaction and autonomous exercise motivation account for this association in sequence.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 712 students (48.9% girls, mean age 12.0 years, SD = 1.8; 366 primary and 346 secondary) from eight schools in Wuhan completed measures of perceived mastery climate, need satisfaction in PE, autonomous exercise motivation, and body self-concept.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A structural equation model with 5,000 bootstrap resamples showed that a stronger mastery climate was associated with higher need satisfaction ( β  = 0.42, p  < 0.001), which predicted more autonomous exercise motivation ( β  = 0.45, p  < 0.001), which in turn predicted a more positive body self-concept ( β  = 0.30, p  < 0.001). The serial indirect effect from climate through needs and motivation to body self-concept was b  = 0.069, 95% CI [0.049, 0.093], about a quarter (23%) of the total association of b  = 0.296, 95% CI [0.211, 0.382]; the direct path remained significant ( β  = 0.12, p  = 0.002). The measurement model was metric invariant across school levels, the three core paths did not differ detectably between primary and secondary students, and girls reported slightly lower body self-concept after adjustment ( β  = -0.07, p  = 0.035).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: These findings connect achievement goal and self-determination perspectives: PE lessons built around self-referenced progress, cooperative learning, and skill mastery may support students' body self-concept partly through their basic psychological needs and their autonomous reasons for moving. Because the data are cross-sectional, the estimated sequence is associational rather than causal, and it identifies motivational climate as a candidate target for interventions aimed at a psychological outcome that is central to adolescent mental health.

items.title: Psychological support for women following perinatal loss: a systematic review of clinical practice guidance.
items.authors: Hefferman-Clarke R, Gregg L, Wittkowski A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: While there is recognition of perinatal mental health worldwide, high income countries are increasingly acknowledging the mental health consequences of perinatal loss (the loss of a baby during pregnancy or shortly after birth). Frameworks and pathways have been developed to improve service provision for women who experience expected distress and/or mental health conditions following perinatal loss. Clinical practice guidelines can offer healthcare professionals direction on how to identify and treat psychological difficulties and distress after a perinatal loss. Typically, these guidelines have medical management as their primary focus, but less is known about the availability of recommendations for the assessment and management of psychological difficulties. Thus, the aim of the current review was to 1) identify perinatal mental health and perinatal loss clinical practice guidelines which contained one or more psychological recommendation(s) relevant to supporting a woman's mental health following perinatal loss, 2) assess the quality of the guidance and 3) synthesize psychological recommendations.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search of literature and guideline databases alongside healthcare organizations concerning maternal and perinatal mental health care was conducted. Relevant guidelines were identified and quality assessed using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation - Global Rating Scale tool. Included recommendations were analyzed through narrative synthesis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Sixteen guidelines met the inclusion criteria. Three had a primary focus on perinatal mental health and the remaining 13 were perinatal loss-specific guidelines. Ten of the included 16 guidelines were quality appraised as "excellent" for methodological quality, four as "good," and two as "average." The extracted recommendations related to psychological assessment, psychological intervention, psychosocial support, service provision, and systemic considerations. Recommendation consistency and specificity varied considerably across guidelines. Overall, recommendations for psychological assessment and longer term follow up were limited.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Allowing space for the natural grieving process can mean that mental health difficulties following perinatal loss are missed. However, the lack of clear recommendations for follow up may hinder women's access to evidence-based intervention, should they need it. Thus, there is a need for a cross-disciplinary clinical practice guideline to be developed which outlines evidence-based recommendations specifically focused on supporting women's wellbeing and mental health following perinatal loss.

items.title: Beyond individual behavior: a multidimensional review of the health, psychological, social, and economic contexts of obesity.
items.authors: Alwulaii AN.

sections.text: Obesity continues to rise worldwide despite unprecedented health awareness and an expanding dieting culture. This narrative review moves beyond an individual-behavioral understanding of obesity by synthesizing evidence on its health, economic, psychological, and social dimensions and proposing a cross-domain framework that grades the evidence supporting each pathway. A structured, non-systematic search of six databases (January 2010-March 2026) identified 57 sources, prioritizing systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and longitudinal studies. Obesity is a chronic, multisystem disease affecting more than 1 billion people, and the recent distinction between clinical and preclinical obesity shifts attention from body size to functional consequences. Its economic burden extends beyond healthcare costs to lost productivity and wage penalties, while household costs, including long-term pharmacotherapy, remain largely unquantified. Obesity and depression show a bidirectional association that may be sustained by internalized weight stigma and shared inflammatory-metabolic pathways. Socially, obesity is associated with employment discrimination, barriers in romantic relationships, and bullying. Although most evidence is observational, these dimensions appear mutually reinforcing, with obesity acting as both an outcome and a contributor, which may explain why behavior-focused interventions alone have not reversed the epidemic. Studies integrating several dimensions within the same population remain scarce, particularly in Arab and Gulf populations, where existing evidence addresses prevalence, cost, stigma, and policy separately. Integrated longitudinal research and multidisciplinary prevention strategies, including in Gulf contexts, are needed.

items.title: Lived Experiences of Pornography Exposure among Adolescents in East Kalimantan, Indonesia: A Qualitative Study.
items.authors: Winarti Y, Shaluhiyah Z, Widjanarko B, Margawati A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Pornography exposure among Indonesian adolescents is a growing concern, as limited sexuality education and cultural taboos restrict open discussion of sexuality related issues. This study aimed to explore adolescents' lived experiences of pornography exposure and its psychological impacts, identify their educational needs, and examine the perspectives of key stakeholders.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This qualitative study was conducted in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, between January and April 2025 following a preliminary screening survey to identify students with diverse exposure histories. Data were collected through two focus group discussions (FGDs) with adolescents and stakeholders, and six in-depth interviews (IDIs) with students. Data were analyzed thematically following Braun and Clarke's framework, with methodological triangulation applied to enhance trustworthiness.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Thirteen participants were involved, consisting of six senior high school students (including two peer educators) and seven stakeholders (two school counselors, one clinical psychologist, two public health academics, one youth task force representative, and one officer from the Population and Family Planning Office). This composition of participants was selected to allow triangulation between adolescents' lived experiences and stakeholders' professional perspectives. Three overarching themes emerged: (1) ambivalent perceptions and lived experiences of pornography, (2) psychological, academic, and social consequences, including intrusive thoughts, sleep disturbance, declining performance, aggression, and imitative risk taking; (3) educational needs and preferences. Adolescents reported curiosity, guilt, secrecy, intrusive thoughts, sleep difficulties, and reduced concentration. They preferred short digital videos and supportive peer led discussions over conventional seminars. Stakeholders emphasized stronger school family collaboration.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Adolescents described pornography exposure as intertwined with curiosity, guilt, and secrecy, alongside perceived difficulties in daily life. Findings support the development of culturally sensitive, peer led digital education with school and family involvement.

items.title: Generative AI Use for Mental Health Support Among Students at a UK University: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Lambert J, Marshall N, Loades M, Gjersoe N, Thomas G, Linton MJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are increasingly used for health information and emotional support, yet little is known about their use for mental health by university students, a population with high digital literacy and elevated mental health need.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To estimate the prevalence of GenAI use for mental health support among respondents to a survey at a single UK university and to identify demographic and well-being characteristics associated with use.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Cross-sectional online survey of students at a large UK university. The primary outcome was self-reported GenAI use for mental health support in the past 6 months. Well-being was assessed using the Short Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale. Associations were examined using multivariable modified Poisson regression to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 22,207 students invited, 2020 responded (response rate 9.1%). Among respondents, 25.0% (n=503) reported GenAI use for mental health support in the past 6 months. The most common reasons were advice when emotionally distressed (n=380, 19.3%), insights into mental health (n=256, 12.7%), and using GenAI as a personal therapist or coach (n=173, 8.6%); 2.7% (n=54) reported using GenAI to seek support when experiencing thoughts of self-harm. Use was more common among students aged 26-29 years, those identifying as Asian, students reporting a declared disability, students enrolled in management programs, and those with lower well-being.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Among respondents at a UK university, approximately one in four reported using GenAI for mental health support. Use was concentrated among students reporting poorer well-being and disability, suggesting that GenAI may function as an informal help-seeking pathway. Universities and health services should anticipate GenAI as a help-seeking pathway and ensure appropriate guidance, integration with existing services, and safeguards to support safe and equitable use.

items.title: Diffuse Argyrophilic Grain Disease With LATE-NC Presenting as Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia and Parkinsonism.
items.authors: Maeda K, Beck G, Shigenobu K, Tarutani A, Yamamoto T, Mori K, Saito Y, Morii E, Hasegawa M, Murayama S.
items.journal: Neuropathology : official journal of the Japanese Society of Neuropathology

sections.text: Argyrophilic grain disease (AGD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by accumulation of argyrophilic grains (AGs), especially in the limbic system. Patients with AGD show a variety of psychiatric symptoms, including cognitive impairment, irritability, and agitation. However, a conclusive diagnosis of AGD requires neuropathological examination by autopsy. Recent studies have suggested that patients with AGD exhibit parkinsonism, which is induced by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. In the present study, we report an autopsy of a diffuse form of AGD that presented with psychiatric symptoms mimicking behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and parkinsonism with a total clinical course of 16 years. Brain imaging of the patient showed generalized cerebral atrophy with mild accentuation in the frontotemporal cortex. These findings are uncommon in patients with bvFTD. Neuropathological examination revealed numerous AGs in broad areas of the brain, including the limbic regions and the neocortex. Neuronal loss due to AGs has also been observed in the substantia nigra. These findings led to the diagnosis of diffuse AGD. Western blot analysis of sarkosyl-insoluble fractions of frozen specimens of the frontal cortex and amygdala showed a predominant doublet band of 37 kDa corresponding to C-terminal tau, in addition to the bands corresponding to full-length tau. Immune electron microscopy revealed phosphorylated tau-positive ribbon-like tau filaments in the frontal cortex and amygdala. Although the clinical symptoms were compatible with bvFTD, AGD should be considered in patients with a prolonged clinical course, atypical neuroradiological findings, or parkinsonism.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Postpartum Period: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Gonçalves Dos Santos G, Mendes Marques de Lima Franco AP, Castilha do Nascimento F, de Oliveira LE, Cunha Silva Lima MJ, Guerra de Oliveira Neto J, Nascimento WSM, Freitas Nascimento MV, Mendes Santos PV, de Almeida Dionizio L, Guerra MJJ, das Neves Carvalho JM, Ribeiro da Fonseca Dias AC, Bettencourt MLS, Pinto Sampaio Costa IC.

sections.text: Background: The use of digital health technologies, such as chatbots and virtual assistants based on artificial intelligence, has grown significantly in maternal health. These tools have been applied at different stages of the pregnancy and postpartum cycle, with emphasis on health education, risk monitoring, breastfeeding support, and mental healthcare. Despite their potential, challenges remain regarding clinical effectiveness, equity of access, and ethical safety. The aim of this study was to map the available evidence regarding the applications of artificial intelligence in pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care, with particular emphasis on conversational agents, virtual assistants, machine learning models, and clinical decision support systems, as well as their potential benefits, limitations, ethical implications, and implementation challenges. Methods: A scoping review was conducted between August and September 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Nursing Database, Latin American and Caribbean Literature in Health Sciences, and Google Scholar. Original articles, reviews, experience reports, and theoretical reflections published in Portuguese, English, or Spanish that addressed the use of digital tools based on artificial intelligence in the pregnancy and postpartum cycle were included. The analysis of the studies was organized into five thematic axes: applications in prenatal care; support during childbirth; postpartum monitoring and breastfeeding; perinatal mental health; and ethical, technical, and implementation challenges. Results: The search identified 6230 records, of which 13 studies were included. Findings indicate that chatbots and virtual assistants show good acceptability, promote health education, and contribute to the early detection of physical and emotional risks. However, most of the studies are exploratory, with methodological limitations, lack of clinical trials, and limited validation in socially vulnerable contexts. Conclusions: Chatbots and artificial intelligence tools are promising resources for perinatal care, particularly as a complement to face-to-face attention. Their consolidation requires robust studies, cost-effectiveness assessments, and public policies that ensure equity and digital inclusion.

items.title: Compassion Fatigue in General and Psychiatric Hospital Nurses: A Systematic Review of Patterns, Determinants, and Consequences.
items.authors: Mahsoon A, Alharthi Y.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Compassion fatigue (CF), commonly discussed alongside burnout and secondary traumatic stress, is an important occupational concern in nursing. General and psychiatric hospital environments expose nurses to different combinations of organizational, emotional, and relational demands. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and compare the reported patterns, determinants, and consequences of compassion fatigue among nurses working in general and psychiatric hospital settings and to identify setting-specific factors relevant to nursing practice and workforce support. Methods: The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 to 2025. Quantitative and qualitative hospital-based nursing studies reporting CF or closely related professional-quality-of-life constructs were eligible. Methodological quality was appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, and findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study designs, instruments, and reporting formats. Results: Eighteen studies were included after screening 302 records identified in the database searches. Moderate-to-high CF-related burden was reported across both general and psychiatric settings, but direct prevalence comparisons were not appropriate because instruments, definitions, and thresholds differed substantially. General-hospital studies more often emphasized workload, high acuity, staffing pressures, sleep disruption, and acute trauma exposure, whereas psychiatric studies more often emphasized moral distress, aggression or workplace violence, stigma, and prolonged emotionally demanding therapeutic relationships. Across settings, CF was associated with poorer psychological and occupational well-being. Conclusions: The available evidence supports setting-sensitive prevention and workforce-support strategies but does not establish that one hospital setting has a uniformly higher prevalence of CF. More consistent definitions, measurement tools, and reporting thresholds are needed to enable reliable cross-setting comparisons.

items.title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation of the Tidal Model Holistic Assessment Instrument to the Brazilian Context.
items.authors: Bessa MM, Lima MVC, Monteiro ARM, Melo JAL, Nascimento EGCD, Carvalho REFL, Oliveira SKP, Freitas RJM.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: The Holistic Assessment, grounded in the Tidal Model, supports person-centered nursing assessment by emphasizing individuals' lived experiences, needs, and personal resources in mental health care. This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Tidal Model Holistic Assessment into Brazilian Portuguese. Methods: This methodological study comprised six stages: translation, synthesis, back-translation, expert evaluation, pretesting, and review by the instrument's original author. Semantic, idiomatic, cultural, and conceptual equivalence were assessed by 11 expert nurses in the first round and seven in the second. The pretest involved 15 mental health service users and 15 nurses, who assessed their comprehension using a five-point scale and provided suggestions for improvement. items.title: Public Stigma and Mental Health Problems: A Comparative Analysis of the General Population and Healthcare Professionals Not Specialized in Mental Health.
items.authors: Liñán-Díaz L, Bernat-Adell MD, Vives-Díaz N, Bernalte-Martí V.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Public stigma towards people with mental health problems persists in both the general population and healthcare settings. However, direct comparisons between these groups remain limited. This study aimed to compare public stigma levels between the Spanish general population and healthcare professionals not specialized in mental health. Methods: An observational, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted in Spain using two independent convenience samples: 404 individuals from the general population and 702 healthcare professionals (646 nurses and 56 physicians). Attitudes were assessed using the Spanish version of the Community Attitudes towards Mental Illness Scale-Short Form (CAMI-S). Group differences were examined, and multiple linear regression was used to identify factors associated with attitudes towards people with mental health problems. Results: Healthcare professionals showed significantly more favourable attitudes than the general population in the overall CAMI-S score and across its three dimensions: integration and contact, social distance, and dangerousness and avoidance. However, the differences were small, suggesting limited practical differences between groups. In the adjusted multivariable analysis, university education, female sex, not having children, personal history of mental health problems, and close contact with people with mental health problems were significantly associated with more favourable attitudes. Healthcare professional status was not significantly associated with CAMI-S scores after adjustment for educational attainment and other covariates. The model explained 14.1% of the variance in CAMI-S scores. Conclusions: More favourable attitudes than the general population were found in the unadjusted comparisons. However, healthcare professional status was not significantly associated with attitudes after adjustment for educational attainment and other covariates. These findings highlight the importance of considering sociodemographic characteristics when interpreting differences in mental health stigma between groups.

items.title: Effectiveness of a Web App-Supported Physical Activity Prescription Strategy Within a Multimodal Lifestyle Intervention in Adults with Cardiometabolic Risk: A Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial.
items.authors: Barceló-Peiró O, Prats-Arimon M, Grau-Feliu A, Feixes-Betriu M, Sanchez-Balcells S, Agüera Z, Sànchez-Ortega MA, Moreno-Arroyo C, Lluch-Canut T, Pérez A, Ventosa-Ruiz A, Bové L, Puig-Llobet M.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Physical inactivity and sedentary behaviour contribute to cardiometabolic disease. This study evaluated the effects of the nine-month multimodal APA-FIT intervention on physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and positive mental health. Methods: In this multicentre randomised controlled trial, 436 adults with moderate or high cardiometabolic risk were randomly allocated (1:1) to APA-FIT or usual care; 425 completed the baseline assessment. Physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and positive mental health were assessed at baseline and nine months using validated questionnaires. Longitudinal outcomes were analysed using mixed-effects models. Results: Total physical activity increased by 935.4 MET min/week in the intervention group, with a significant between-group difference in change (β = 986.6; 95% CI 559.8-1413.4; p < 0.001). Sedentary time decreased by 0.85 h/day (β = -0.76; 95% CI -1.26 to -0.26; p = 0.003). Positive mental health improved over time but showed no significant between-group difference in change (β = 0.043; 95% CI -1.139 to 1.225; p = 0.943). Exploratory intervention-group web-app data showed increased recorded mobility and mobility-goal achievement, consistently high sedentary-behaviour goal achievement, and declining exercise-session recording. Conclusions: Compared with usual care, APA-FIT increased self-reported physical activity and reduced self-reported sedentary time in adults at cardiometabolic risk, without an intervention-specific effect on positive mental health.

items.title: Patterns of Liver Injury in Hospitalized Patients with Anaplasmosis in Minnesota and Wisconsin.
items.authors: Nordstrom CW, Penrice D, Ward M, Milovanovic T, Dumic I.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Liver test abnormalities are common in anaplasmosis, but their pattern has not been characterized. We aimed to describe the frequency, pattern, and severity of liver injury and acute hepatitis in hospitalized patients. Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of a previously described cohort of adults hospitalized with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed anaplasmosis in Minnesota and Wisconsin, USA, between 2014 and 2024. After excluding patients with alcohol use disorder, tick-borne coinfection, or other causes of liver injury, we classified the pattern of injury by R factor in patients with elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or alkaline phosphatase (ALP). We compared patients with acute hepatitis and those with isolated abnormalities.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 78 eligible patients with liver tests, 64 (82.1%) had at least one abnormality, most often of aspartate aminotransferase (AST; 92.2%). Among 50 patients with elevated ALT or ALP, the pattern was cholestatic in 56.0%, mixed in 36.0%, and hepatocellular in 8.0%; 14 patients had isolated AST elevation. Most elevations were mild, and no patient developed acute liver failure. Patients with acute hepatitis (n = 14, 21.9%) more often had elevated ALP than those with isolated abnormalities (85.7% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.030), whereas the pattern of injury did not differ.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Liver involvement in hospitalized patients with anaplasmosis is common and may present as acute hepatitis or as isolated liver test abnormalities. It is usually mild, predominantly cholestatic or mixed, and does not progress to liver failure. Isolated AST elevation is frequent and may partly reflect muscle injury.

items.title: Psychological factors and their relative importance in occupational burnout among healthcare workers.
items.authors: Zhang P, Zhang C, Zhu Z, Zhao Y, Ai Z, Shi J, Chen F.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: To quantify the relative contributions of internal and external psychological variables to occupational burnout among healthcare workers, providing a quantitative basis for formulating precise organizational intervention strategies.

sections.heading: Participants and methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 417 healthcare workers from 3 hospitals. Dominance analysis was employed to calculate the relative importance of perceived stress, work-family conflict, resilience, psychological distress, and social support in predicting occupational burnout.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Dominance analysis showed that, among psychological demands, perceived stress (38.12%) and work-family conflict (23.73%) had the largest relative explanatory contributions to occupational burnout, while psychological distress contributed 14.80%. Among psychological resources, resilience accounted for 15.95% of the relative importance, and social support accounted for 7.40%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Burnout prevention strategies for healthcare workers may benefit from addressing perceived stress and work-family conflict, while also considering resilience and social support as relevant psychological resources.

items.title: Effect of workplace incivility on nurses' health outcomes: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Wang CH, Tseng YH, Cheng WJ, Lee FC, Pien LC.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Workplace incivility is increasingly recognized as a key occupational stressor in nursing. However, few studies have explored its independent association with nurse health after adjustment for established psychosocial work characteristics. This study examined the associations of workplace incivility from colleagues and supervisors with nurses' self-rated health, burnout, and mental health status after adjusting for job control, psychological job demands, and workplace justice.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted between October and December 2022 at a medical center in northern Taiwan. Full-time registered nurses completed a self-administered questionnaire. A total of 900 valid responses were analyzed (response rate, 84.0%). The questionnaire assessed workplace incivility from colleagues and supervisors, personal burnout, mental health status, self-rated health, and psychosocial work characteristics (job control, psychological job demands, and workplace justice). The chi-square test and multivariable logistic regression were used to examine potential associations between workplace incivility and health outcomes after adjustment for demographic and psychosocial work characteristics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of poor mental health, high personal burnout, and poor self-rated health was higher in nurses with high incivility exposure than in those with low incivility exposure (51.8% vs. 30.0%, 55.3% vs. 40.1%, and 20.4% vs. 11.9%, respectively). After adjustment for psychosocial work characteristics and demographic factors, high workplace incivility remained significantly associated with poor mental health, high personal burnout, and poor self-rated health. High psychological job demands were also significantly associated with increased risks of personal burnout, poor mental health, and poor self-rated health.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Workplace incivility appears to be significantly associated with adverse health outcomes in nurses, independent of psychosocial work characteristics and demographic factors. Furthermore, high psychological job demands may be significantly associated with personal burnout, poor mental health, and poor self-rated health in nurses.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.text: The findings highlight workplace incivility as a key occupational health problem in nursing. Strategies to address workplace incivility and psychological job demands and promote a healthier work environment may support nurses' mental health and overall well-being. This study may guide nurse managers and policymakers in developing organizational strategies to support workplace health and safety.

items.title: More than a room: barriers and unmet needs of Mental Health Nurse Consultants in general hospitals.
items.authors: Li H, Li J, Xie R, Zhou C, Ye J, Chen J, Huang X, Luo S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychiatric comorbidity is common among inpatients in general hospitals, making Mental Health Nurse Consultants (MHNCs) important providers of integrated psychological care. However, evidence regarding the practical barriers affecting MHNC role implementation remains limited, particularly in resource-constrained settings. This study aimed to explore the barriers and unmet needs experienced by MHNCs in Chinese general hospitals.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted at a tertiary general hospital in China in September 2024. Nine purposively sampled participants-including hospital administrators, physicians, nursing managers, and MHNCs-participated in a focus group interview. Data were analysed using descriptive thematic analysis with an independent multi-coder approach, with analytic rigour enhanced through investigator triangulation and reflexive team consensus.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Five themes were identified: (1) structural workload and resource constraints; (2) role ambiguity and limited professional recognition; (3) clinical complexity and decision-making strain; (4) relational stress and information asymmetry; and (5) aspirations for role development. Participants highlighted that insufficient protected time, lack of dedicated consultation space, and unclear role boundaries constrained effective care delivery and interdisciplinary collaboration.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Despite the recognized clinical value of MHNCs, organizational and structural barriers continue to limit role sustainability and effectiveness in general hospitals. Institutional support, including protected working time, standardized workload documentation, dedicated consultation spaces, and formal integration into multidisciplinary teams, may strengthen the implementation of MHNC services and support high-quality integrated mental health care.

items.title: Consciousness, complexity, and clinical implications.
items.authors: Ferrucci R, Corti S, Blandini F, Brambilla P, Bonivento C, Cappa SF, Crippa M, Faggin F, Ferini-Strambi L, Gallese V, Giacchetti M, Manzotti R, Massimini M, Oliveri S, Pezzoli G, Priori A, Stocco M, Stigliani D, Barbieri S.

sections.text: Consciousness remains one of science's most challenging problems because it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a single function, computation, or behavior; it also refers to the presence and organization of subjective experience. This position paper integrates clinical neurology, neurophysiology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, embodied cognition, moral neuroscience, theoretical physics, philosophy of mind, and neurotechnology. We argue that, despite major advances in identifying neural correlates, computational models, and behavioral markers, contemporary consciousness research has not resolved the explanatory gap between objective description and subjective experience. We propose that claims about consciousness at neurophysiological, embodied, cognitive, social, and ontological levels should be coordinated through explicit cross-level constraints rather than merged into a single unitary theory. These domains have different evidential roles and are not all constituents of consciousness. Perturbational measures of cortical complexity, including the Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) and its state-transition variant (PCIst), support assessment of preserved conscious capacity in studied human populations. They do not independently determine a clinical diagnosis or phenomenal content. Evidence from aphasia, sleep, anesthesia, and disorders of consciousness also demonstrates dissociations among language, wakefulness, behavioral responsiveness, and conscious experience. Perspectives from embodied simulation, mind-object identity, quantum information, and the philosophy of physics are treated here as heuristic stress tests rather than as mechanistic accounts; they keep open foundational questions concerning subjectivity, representation, and the role of the observer. We advocate constrained pluralism, a methodological framework in which consciousness is conceptualized as an integrated, embodied, relational, and temporally extended process. Such an approach provides a coherent foundation for future research while strengthening the dialogue between neuroscience, clinical practice, philosophy, and neuroethics.

items.title: Clinical Profile, Previous Diabetic Ketoacidosis, and Hospital Length of Stay in Adults Admitted to Intensive Care: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
items.authors: Mikačić M, Šantić R, Kumrić M, Kovačić V, Krnić M, Tičinović Kurir T, Božić J.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: The clinical history preceding diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and the acute hospital course may reflect different vulnerabilities. We examined factors associated with previous DKA and total hospital length of stay in adults admitted to intensive care. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 91 unique adults admitted during 2021-2025. Firth logistic regression examined previous DKA among 68 patients with established diabetes. Negative binomial regression with HC3 robust inference examined total hospital stay. A separate post hoc Firth model examined severe acid-base presentation. Results: Previous DKA was documented in 28/68 patients (41.2%) and was associated with established type 1 diabetes (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.18-39.83) and recorded psychiatric disorder (aOR 7.35, 95% CI 1.92-36.47). Infection-related presentation was associated with longer stay (adjusted incidence rate ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.07-1.82; p = 0.013), with standardized means of 11.4 versus 8.1 days. Newly diagnosed diabetes was associated with lower odds of severe acid-base presentation in the exploratory model (aOR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.67). No in-hospital deaths occurred. Conclusions: Previous DKA and hospital stay showed different patterns of association. The estimates were imprecise and apply to a small ICU-selected population. The post hoc severity finding requires replication. These observational associations do not establish causation or support individual prediction.

items.title: Mental Health Under Forced Migration: A Process-Oriented Framework Linking Structural Strain, Emotional Activation, and Resource Dynamics.
items.authors: Zipper-Weber V.

sections.text: Forced migration is an ongoing trajectory rather than a single event, with mental-health consequences shaped by changing legal, material, social and service conditions. Although established models connect post-migration stressors with psychological processes and multilevel support, greater temporal and operational precision is needed. This conceptual synthesis develops a hypothesis-generating, process-oriented framework integrating ecological and post-migration stress perspectives, resource theories, refugee evidence on coping and control, and multilevel support. It proposes a conditional sequence in which threat-related appraisal and emotional activation may be followed by goal-directed action, help-seeking, avoidance or withdrawal depending on perceived control, safety, response efficacy and feasible pathways. Where sustained effort occurs, its implications may depend on realised resource returns and recovery opportunities. Limited returns, additional loss or insufficient recovery are hypothesised to contribute to later fatigue or distress, but this temporal pathway remains untested. Translationally, the framework distinguishes referral initiation from completed contact and continuity and organises support as overlapping functions encompassing low-threshold stabilisation, community support, indicated treatment and crisis care, and service navigation. Four propositions formulate conditional and temporally ordered relationships for future empirical evaluation. The framework provides a basis for longitudinal and implementation research and repeated context-sensitive reassessment, not a validated clinical instrument or substitute for structural intervention.

The framework provides a basis for longitudinal and implementation research and repeated context-sensitive reassessment, not a validated clinical instrument or substitute for structural intervention.

items.title: Built Environment and Mental Health Inequalities: An Integrative Agenda for Environmental Epidemiology.
items.authors: White R, Guglielmino D, Capaccioli F, Mariani D, Greco E, Miani A, Piscitelli P, Lippi F.

sections.text: Homes and neighbourhoods are modifiable determinants of mental health, yet translating environmental evidence into equitable prevention requires more than identifying associations between individual exposures and psychological outcomes. This Perspective proposes an evaluation agenda that connects three questions for any residential intervention: what changes in exposure, how residents experience that change, and who can obtain and retain its benefits. We define mental health inequalities as unequal exposure, unequal capacity to benefit, and unequal outcomes, and position the agenda against environmental psychology, ecosocial theory, neighbourhood-effects research, greenspace pathway models, and implementation frameworks, each of which typically addresses one question while treating the others as background. Drawing on purposively selected conceptual, observational, and intervention studies, we provide an operational measurement core with example instruments, timing, and sample-size considerations; guidance on trade-offs between internal and ecological validity; a worked example of a refurbishment evaluation that follows residents who move; and recommendations for reporting and for informing housing, planning, and public health decisions. Building certification should be treated as an implementation resource rather than a surrogate for demonstrated mental health benefit, and biophilic design should be evaluated through specified environmental changes. Causal uncertainty, housing affordability, and distributional consequences should remain central to evaluation.

items.title: Health Determinants and the Development of a Multi-Domain Risk Assessment and Psychological Stratification Framework for Personalized Prevention in Working-Age Adults: The DELPHI (Digital Engagement for Lifelong Prevention and Health Improvement) Project.
items.authors: Iacono Isidoro S, Siotto M, Germanotta M, Guerrini A, Papa MA, Habib V, Campisi S, Bruschetta R, Maiorana MV, Parnasso F, Caci B, Polizzi C, Aprile IG, Tartarisco G.

sections.heading: Background/objective
sections.text: Non-communicable diseases and mental health conditions impose a growing burden on working-age adults, yet prevention strategies remain fragmented and rarely personalized. This study describes the development of an evidence-informed framework integrating multi-domain health assessment and psychological risk stratification to support personalized prevention in adults aged 18-65 years.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: National behavioral surveillance data (PASSI 2023-2024) and occupational disease data (INAIL 2024) were examined to inform the framework. Validated assessment instruments were selected across relevant health domains according to their applicability to the target population. A user-centered and participatory design approach was also incorporated into the DELPHI (Digital Engagement for Lifelong Prevention and Health Improvement) project.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The epidemiological evidence highlighted persistent behavioral risk factors and social inequalities among working-age adults. The resulting framework comprises seven assessment domains, integrating validated instruments to characterize participants' health status and modifiable risk factors. Psychological risk indicators were used to define two personalized prevention pathways, "Maintenance" and "Rebalancing", with periodic reassessment.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The DELPHI framework integrates multi-domain health assessment with psychological risk-based personalization to support preventive interventions in working-age adults. The clinical trial is ongoing; its outcomes, usability and effectiveness will be evaluated upon completion of the project.

items.title: Multi-scale feature fusion and neural architecture search for electroencephalography-based affective-state recognition in public benchmark datasets.
items.authors: Guan C, Wang Y.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based affective-state recognition may provide an objective neurophysiological complement to self-report scales and behavioral observations, but robust modeling remains difficult because EEG signals are non-stationary, temporally heterogeneous, and strongly subject-dependent.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This study evaluated MFANet, a multi-scale feature fusion and neural architecture search-enhanced framework for binary classification of valence, arousal, and dominance. MFANet combines parallel one-dimensional convolutional branches with different receptive fields, channel-wise attention for adaptive feature recalibration, and a neural architecture search-guided long short-term memory module for temporal modeling. The framework was evaluated on the public DEAP and DREAMER datasets using five-fold, trial-grouped subject-dependent cross-validation in which all windows from one stimulus trial remained in the same outer fold and all data-dependent operations were confined to the corresponding training data.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In DEAP ablation experiments, the complete model achieved mean accuracies of 97.20 ± 1.63% for valence, 97.32 ± 1.27% for arousal, and 97.14 ± 1.21% for dominance. Compared with the basic convolutional-recurrent baseline, multi-scale feature fusion and the searched recurrent module improved average accuracy by 10.17 and 10.87 percentage points, respectively, corresponding to relative gains of 12.5% and 13.4%. In participant-level paired comparisons based on the archived participant-level values, MFANet exceeded the dynamic graph convolutional neural network (DGCNN) by 4.13, 3.39, and 3.71 percentage points; bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were 3.29-5.15, 2.56-4.38, and 2.74-4.85, and all Holm-adjusted p-values were <0.001. A DEAP channel-count sensitivity analysis indicated that the full 32-channel montage changed accuracy by less than 0.4 percentage points relative to the prespecified 14-channel montage.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: These findings suggest that joint multi-scale representation learning and adaptive recurrent architecture selection can improve benchmark EEG affective-state recognition. Because the analysis used public healthy-volunteer datasets and self-reported affective labels, the framework should be regarded as a computational method for future clinical validation rather than a diagnostic tool.

items.title: Refining psychological phenotyping in chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome: the potential role of the p factor.
items.authors: Wu S, Ding L, Wu L.

sections.text: Chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) presents with variable pelvic pain, urinary and sexual symptoms, and functional impairment. Psychological factors are established components of assessment, and UPOINT has brought psychosocial involvement into phenotype-directed care. The unresolved question is whether modelling shared psychopathology improves on the combined use of established assessments. The general factor of psychopathology (p) is a candidate representation of shared covariance across broad psychiatric domains; its clinical utility in CP/CPPS is unestablished. A single latent score does not inherently distinguish severe symptoms within one domain from moderate symptoms across several domains. We separate measurement indicators, p, specific psychological processes, contextual information and future outcomes. A four-stage roadmap addresses measurement development, longitudinal interpretation, incremental prediction and clinical translation. Comparisons must distinguish the contribution of additional assessment content from that of a p representation using identical information. Direct assessment of actionable problems and individualized clinical formulation remain essential. Predictive improvement would not itself establish that using p improves care, and a single output score does not reduce assessment burden. If p adds little reproducible and clinically meaningful value, simpler established measures should remain preferred.
