items.title: Configurational pathways associated with flourishing among Russian university students: an exploratory fsQCA study of transilience in a permacrisis context.
items.authors: Akbasheva A, Chen C, Hao Y.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Prolonged adversity (permacrisis) presents novel demands for young adults, shifting focus from deficit-oriented mental health models to understanding how positive transformation occurs. Transilience, distinguished from resilience by its focus on systemic reorganization rather than homeostatic return to baseline, defines the perceived capacity to persist, adapt flexibly, and transform positively amid sustained threats. However, little is known about how specific combinations of these components relate to mental health outcomes.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A preliminary qualitative conceptualization (grounded theory) with 27 students purposively selected for narratives of positive transformation in response to crisis first informed the transilience model and its survey operationalization; fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis was then applied to a separate sample of Russian university students (N = 146) to test two hypotheses: (H1) transformability is consistently present across multiple equifinal configurations associated with flourishing; (H2) configurational structures differ depending on whether students appraise permacrisis aspects as major threats or manageable challenges.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Five equifinal configurations were consistently associated with flourishing (solution coverage = 0.804, consistency = 0.849). No single condition was necessary and multiple pathways were identified. The H1 prediction regarding the universal presence of transformability was not supported across the full set of solutions. Transformability did not enter the socially-mediated pathways but was consistently present in autonomous configurations. Cross-group analyses further supported H2; students' stressor appraisal was associated with qualitatively different configurational solutions to well-being, even within the same macro-context.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This configurational analysis examined transilience as a complex, multi-component construct by identifying several distinct configurations associated with flourishing rather than a single universal pattern, informing program design and theoretical advancement. The consistent co-occurrence of transformability within autonomous configurations is compatible with a compensatory account, which we advance as a hypothesis for future longitudinal research.

items.title: Pandemic management and preparedness in Austria: experiences and expectations across society from a vignette-based qualitative study.
items.authors: Vorstandlechner M, Harlfinger J, Koscher-Kien C, Morasek K, Schneckenreither G, Zauner G, Ritschl V, Popper N, Gartlehner G, Stamm T.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Pandemic preparedness depends not only on biomedical capacity, but also on public trust, legitimacy, communication, and the perceived fairness of crisis measures. This vignette-based qualitative study explored how participants from diverse professional and social backgrounds in Austria reason about priorities, responsibilities, and appropriate responses in future pandemic scenarios.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 28 participants and analysed the transcripts using inductive thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants understood pandemic governance as a societal and political challenge rather than a purely technical one. Five themes were identified: the critical role of independent and interdisciplinary experts; communication as an essential component of trust, adherence, and error culture in pandemic management; the pandemic as a mirror of broader societal weaknesses, including fragmented governance and declining solidarity; data governance as a foundation for informed decision-making; and education and mental health as priorities in pandemic response.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The findings suggest that future pandemic preparedness requires strengthening institutional transparency, coordinated decision-making, inclusive communication, usable health data, and sustained attention to psychosocial consequences before crises emerge.

items.title: Development and validation of the personal recovery scale (ReConnect) for mental health in Ethiopia.
items.authors: Fekadu W, Alem A, Asher L, Mihretu A, Roberts T, Kiross D, Feyasa MB, Mulushewa A, Misganaw E, Teferra S, Shibre T, Malla A, Cohen A, Lund C, Fekadu A, Hanlon C.
items.journal: International journal of mental health systems

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: To develop and validate a mental health personal recovery measure for people with severe mental health conditions (MHCs) in Ethiopia that is grounded in their recovery journey.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study stages were: reviewing existing measures; qualitative exploration of the concept in Ethiopia (n = 25 interviews); expert workshops (n = 3 involving 28 experts); cognitive interviewing for semantic and content validity (n = 20); pilot study for item reduction and exploratory factor analysis (n = 213) and parallel analysis to determine the dimensional structure (n = 213); and assessment of construct (confirmatory factor analysis) and construct validity in an independent sample (n = 401), and test-retest reliability in a sub-sample (n = 48). Construct validity was assessed against symptom severity and disability.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants gave greater emphasis to social recovery than self-actualisation or empowerment; hence, no existing measures had face validity. We piloted 26 items from existing measures and 19 newly developed items. The draft measure was unidimensional, explaining 71% of variance, and had item-test correlations > 0.58. Item reduction resulted in 20-item scale, ReConnect (Recovery and Connection Scale). In the validation study, ReConnect was unidimensional with acceptable goodness of fit indices and test-retest reliability and correlated significantly with symptom severity and functioning.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: ReConnect is a valid and reliable measure of personal recovery in Ethiopia. It has potential applicability to other similar settings where the community has a greater role in the recovery journey.

items.title: Factors that facilitate or impede the ability of individuals with mental-physical multimorbidity to access healthcare: A qualitative study.
items.authors: Gabet M, Dubé S, Kim A, L'Espérance A, Breton M, Sasseville M, Rivet S, Dufour S, Brochu M, Duhoux A, Paquette JS, Bédard M, Menear M.

sections.text: People living with co-existing mental and chronic physical health conditions (i.e. mental-physical multimorbidity) often have multiple, evolving health needs that require timely access to care. However, little is known about the factors that facilitate or impede their ability to access care. This qualitative descriptive study explored the perspectives of adults living with mental-physical multimorbidity in Quebec (Canada) on the factors that facilitate or hinder their abilities to access care. We conducted 26 individual semi-structured interviews with people who self-reported living with mental-physical multimorbidity. Interview transcripts were analyzed using a mixed inductive-deductive thematic analysis approach, guided by Levesque et al.'s (2013) framework on access to care. Thematic analysis identified eight themes capturing factors influencing access to care. Two themes related to the ability to perceive the need for care: (i) self-awareness and familiarity with services (facilitator) and (ii) internalized beliefs of being a low priority (barrier). Three themes related to the ability to seek care: (iii) self-advocacy (facilitator), (iv) mistrust toward the mental health public system (barrier) and (v) constrained personal autonomy due to the effort required to access care (barrier). Two other themes concerned the ability to reach care: (vi) personal mobility and availability of transportation and (vii) lack of occupational flexibility (both barriers). A last theme related to the ability to pay for care: (viii) lack of financial resources (barrier). These findings underscore potential significant inequities in access to care, through the lens of different abilities reported by individuals with mental-physical multimorbidity.

items.title: Biopsychosocial Mechanisms Linking Maternal Ultra-Processed Food Consumption During Pregnancy to Infant Development: A Prospective Longitudinal Observational Cohort Study Protocol (BRiDge-I).
items.authors: Kokkinaki T, Perdikogianni C, Vrekoussis T, Sarri K, Roumeliotaki T, Petrakis A, Kyprakis I, Kondylakis H, Hatzidaki E, Symvoulakis EK.

sections.text: Early neurodevelopment is influenced by a complex interplay of genetic, biological, and environmental factors, including maternal nutrition. High maternal consumption of ultra-processed foods (UPF) during pregnancy has been associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, poorer maternal mental health, and potentially less favourable neurodevelopmental outcomes in offspring. However, the association between maternal UPF consumption during pregnancy and infant development, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remains unclear. This proposed prospective longitudinal observational cohort study aims to investigate the association between maternal UPF consumption during pregnancy and infant developmental outcomes at 9 months of age, while exploring potential biological and psychosocial mechanisms underlying this relationship. At least 280 mother-infant dyads will be recruited from the Obstetrics Clinic of the University General Hospital of Heraklion, Crete, Greece. Maternal UPF intake will be assessed using the GR-UPFAST, a validated tool based on the NOVA classification system, complemented by a validated, culture-specific Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Infant development will be evaluated using the Ages and Stages Questionnaires-Third Version (ASQ-3). Exploratory measures will include the FIB-4 score, neonatal heart rate variability (HRV), and maternal psychosocial well-being. We hypothesize that higher maternal UPF consumption during pregnancy will be associated with less favorable infant developmental outcomes. The findings may inform nutritional recommendations and early preventive strategies aimed at promoting optimal infant development.

items.title: Connection, belonging, and agency: A qualitative study of stateless community spaces and the mental wellbeing of stateless people.
items.authors: Oppenheim E, O'Driscoll C, Brady F.

sections.text: Statelessness, affecting an estimated fifteen million people globally, has significant mental health impacts. Largely excluded from formal provision, stateless people often turn to community spaces, delivered by and for stateless people for purposes such as advocacy, legal assistance, education, or community connection. Although previous research suggests these spaces benefit the mental wellbeing of stateless people, few studies explore this topic. This study explores the mental wellbeing experiences of organisers and members of stateless community spaces and examines barriers and facilitators to running them effectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve people with lived experience of statelessness who had participated in or organised these spaces. Data was analysed using thematic analysis. Three themes emerged: Personal Journeys in Community Spaces; Making It Work; and Navigating Challenging Systems. Results demonstrated that community spaces represent a vital tool in supporting stateless people's mental wellbeing by offering experiences of connection, belonging, and agency systematically denied to stateless people in wider society. Participants identified stateless leadership and practical support, such as legal and financial assistance, as essential to effective community spaces. Mental health support was usually offered indirectly by community spaces rather than through explicit provision, and while participants valued the wellbeing benefits of these spaces, they felt more dedicated mental health support was needed for both members and organisers. Community spaces were shown to be operating without adequate funding and in challenging political environments, often at considerable personal cost to organisers. Lack of funding forced trade-offs regarding which activities to prioritise, making further mental health provision challenging. Increased sustained funding is urgently needed for stateless community spaces to maintain existing activities and to develop mental health support.

Results demonstrated that community spaces represent a vital tool in supporting stateless people's mental wellbeing by offering experiences of connection, belonging, and agency systematically denied to stateless people in wider society. Participants identified stateless leadership and practical support, such as legal and financial assistance, as essential to effective community spaces. Mental health support was usually offered indirectly by community spaces rather than through explicit provision, and while participants valued the wellbeing benefits of these spaces, they felt more dedicated mental health support was needed for both members and organisers. Community spaces were shown to be operating without adequate funding and in challenging political environments, often at considerable personal cost to organisers. Lack of funding forced trade-offs regarding which activities to prioritise, making further mental health provision challenging. Increased sustained funding is urgently needed for stateless community spaces to maintain existing activities and to develop mental health support.

summary.text: Lack of funding forced trade-offs regarding which activities to prioritise, making further mental health provision challenging. Increased sustained funding is urgently needed for stateless community spaces to maintain existing activities and to develop mental health support.

items.title: EQ-5D-5L Measurement in Bulgarian Community Pharmacies: A Cross-Sectional Study of Published Patient Data and a New Pharmacist Survey to Inform a Prospective Feasibility Study.
items.authors: Vutova Y, Georgiev S, Krastev H, Slavchev G, Djambazov S.

sections.text: Bulgaria lacks routine EQ-5D-5L data collection and a national value set, so domestic health technology assessment relies on imported utility values. This study evaluated whether existing evidence justifies a feasibility study of routine EQ-5D-5L measurement in community pharmacies. In this cross-sectional study, reported according to STROBE, we analysed secondary data from a previously published pharmacy-based patient survey and primary data from a new pharmacist survey on questionnaire-based mental health screening, and used both to specify its design. In the source study ( n = 119), complete EQ-5D-5L data were obtained from all enrolled participants (mean utility 0.72, 95% CI 0.679-0.756), with directionally consistent known-groups differences; the number of patients approached, administration time and acceptability were not reported. Among surveyed pharmacists ( n = 105; convenience sample, response rate not calculable), 80.0% would undertake training and 75.2% would participate in a screening service given clear referral procedures; leading constraints were lack of confidential space (79.0%), time (64.8%) and trained staff (56.2%). Familiarity with PHQ-9/GAD-7 was associated with greater willingness (risk difference 20.5 percentage points, 95% CI 3.9-35.9). EQ-5D-5L-specific readiness was not assessed. Because key feasibility parameters are unknown, a prospective multicentre feasibility study is justified; its endpoints and provisional progression criteria are specified.

items.title: Occupational stress and its association with nurses productivity in the Buea Health District, Cameroon: A cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Eni AT, Takang KT, Kibu OD, Ketum TC, Nicholas T.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Occupational stress is a major concern among healthcare workers, particularly nurses, due to its negative impacts on mental health and productivity. Nurses face multiple stressors including heavy workloads, long hours, exposure to infectious diseases, and the emotional toll of patient care. This study assessed the prevalence of occupational stress and its association with nurses' productivity in the Buea Health District, Cameroon.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A hospital‑based cross‑sectional study was conducted among 301 nurses using a structured questionnaire to collect socio‑demographic data, occupational stress, and productivity measures. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Chi‑squared tests, and linear regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among the 301 nurses included in the study, 250 (83.1%) were female, and the mean age was 26.3 ± 5.0 years. The prevalence of occupational stress was 46.0% (138/301). Linear regression analysis showed that occupational stress was significantly associated with lower task performance (B = -0.24, 95% CI: -0.29 to -0.18; p < 0.001), lower contextual performance (B = -0.27, 95% CI: -0.36 to -0.18; p < 0.001), and lower overall work productivity (B = -0.56, 95% CI: -0.71 to -0.41; p < 0.001). Occupational stress explained 19.5%, 10.9%, and 15.9% of the variance in task performance, contextual performance, and overall work productivity, respectively. No significant association was observed between occupational stress and counterproductive work behaviour (B = 0.05, 95% CI: -0.04 to 0.14; p = 0.260). Several sociodemographic factors, including sex, marital status, educational level, age, and monthly income, were independently associated with specific dimensions of work productivity.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Occupational stress was associated with reduced task, contextual, and overall work productivity among nurses, but not with counterproductive work behaviour. Interventions aimed at reducing occupational stress may help enhance workforce productivity in healthcare settings.

items.title: What do the social determinants of mental health mean for psychiatry, psychology and law?
items.authors: Wilson K.
items.journal: Psychiatry, psychology, and law : an interdisciplinary journal of the Australian and New Zealand Association of Psychiatry, Psychology and Law

sections.text: The social determinants of mental health refer to the way in which structural and systemic factors and daily living conditions (such as poverty, inequality, education, unemployment, work stress, discrimination, housing etc) shape mental health and wellbeing. Such a preventative and public health-focused approach stands in contrast to, and arguably challenges the validity of, the dominant individualised biomedical response to mental ill-health and the expertise of mental health professionals. This article explores what the social determinants of mental health mean for psychiatrists, psychologists and lawyers conceptually (in terms of embracing a truly balanced biopsychosocial model); in clinical practice (including through recruitment and training, social determinants assessments, health-justice partnerships and social prescribing); and with respect to psychiatrists, psychologists and lawyers as advisers in law and policy development. It also discusses a new Public Mental Health Framework and how it can be used to prevent mental ill-health and promote wellbeing.

items.title: Informing Digital Career Transition and Mental Health Support Services Implementation: Perspectives of Active and Retired European Elite Athletes.
items.authors: Di Rocco F, Romagnoli C, Ciaccioni S, Demarie S, Doupona M, Capranica L, Padua E, Guidotti F.

sections.text: This cross-sectional study explored the perceived challenges and needs of a convenience sample of European elite athletes regarding multilevel support services (dual career, mental health, and career retirement). Athletes recruited through the networks of the EU-funded "PORTAL" project partners in five European countries completed a 50-item semi-structured electronic questionnaire. Information relative to career path, career challenges and needs, and the perceived relevance, availability, satisfaction, frequency of provision, and possible digital implementation of 12 potential career support services were considered for analysis. Respondents (n = 136; 46% female; 44% retired; 75% Olympic/World) highlighted difficulties during their athletic and dual career paths, with limited formal recognition from sport (41%) and academic/vocational environments (43%), and inadequate preparation for retirement (48%). For retirement preparation, career transitions and mental health support services were considered crucial (5 pts/6), although the perceived effectiveness of currently available services was low (3 pts/6). Among the 12 evaluated services, workshops, career development/networking, financial planning, and mental health counselling were rated as the most relevant (4 pts/5). Most services (10/12) were reported as available by fewer than half of respondents (range: 20-44%), with a generally perceived low satisfaction (range: 2.5-3.2 pts/5). Positive perceptions emerged for possible digital implementation of all 12 services (range: 3.8-4.2 pts/5), with a service-dependent preferred frequency of provision varying from weekly to occasional. Considering the importance of multidimensional support systems for addressing practical, psychological, and emotional retirement-related challenges, although descriptive of the present sample and not generalizable to all European elite athletes, these end-user-informed findings may guide the development and implementation of a digital platform supporting athletes throughout their dual-career and retirement pathways and life beyond sport.
